events.[bandyci_na_trakcie].scenes.[band.t: You leave them in the ditch to think their lives over. On one of them you found something that pulses warm in your hand. You move on before either of them comes round.

You leap into the bushes, and the nettles lash your calves worse than the master ever lashed your back. The brigands howl after you, but none of them can be bothered to give chase. You go the long way round through the forest and only get back onto the road beyond the hill.

Round a bend in the road two strapping louts with sticks climb out of the roadside bushes, stinking like a wet sheepskin. "Hand over your purse, young master, and you'll keep walking on your own two legs!" They've likely never seen a blade in their lives, but they know how to swing a stick.

events.[blednik_w_szkle].scenes.[blednik.t: The wisp goes out with a hiss, and a small figure in a cap sinks into a shard. The glass all around falls quiet.
You scurry off over the glass, which creaks underfoot. The fire behind you doesn't give chase. It just watches.
On the glassy ground dances a little fire that isn't fire. It's mirrored in every shard, as if there were a thousand of them. As you come closer, they all go out but one, which flies straight at you.

events.[cisza].scenes.[cisza_droga].text.t: The road winds between birches, birds screech in the undergrowth, and the only enemy is a stone in your boot. The day passes quietly, knock on wood.

events.[dym_nad_stocznia].scenes.[dym_na.t: A thick column of smoke rises over the Shipyard. Someone is bawling orders, someone runs with buckets, and then it all goes quiet. Somebody's boat has burned down to the waterline. Nobody asks whose fault it was.

events.[dzieci_i_smola].scenes.[dzieci_i.t: Children are playing ships on the shore: one is captain, three are the crew, and the smallest, the fourth, plays the storm. All their faces are smeared with tar. They freeze mid-shout when they see you, then go back to the game as if you were just the wind.

events.[dziecko_z_listem].scenes.[dzieck.t: A dirty-faced boy hands you a folded scrap of paper. "From a gentleman who didn't give his name." You unfold it. One word: "Beware." The boy has no idea who sent him, but he's sorry he got nothing for it. You give him an apple and he vanishes into the crowd.

events.[dzik_na_sciezce].scenes.[dzik_na.t: The boar goes down heavily, and the smell of resin and blood hangs in the air. A beast like that could feed a village.
You scramble up onto a fallen trunk, and the boar trudges on with dignity and contempt.
A boar the size of a calf bursts out of the undergrowth, bristles like a scrubbing brush. It snorts once and charges.

events.[gapowicz_na_dziobie].scenes.[gap.t: A dirty hand creeps out from under the tarpaulin in the bow, then another, then a whole face with an indignant look. "I only shifted over a bit, sir, it was cramped over there." The helmsman shrugs. The stowaway ducks back, and an hour later off-key whistling starts coming from under the tarpaulin.

events.[handlarz_z_lodzi].scenes.[handla.t: A boat at the jetty is piled with a stall's worth of goods: pegs, hooks, salt, powder, even rusty anchors. The trader winks as if he can tell you're new. "From the mainland? I've got everything your wagons lost."

events.[handlarz_z_zaulka].scenes.[handl.t: A man with a coat full of pockets emerges from the shadow of an alley. "Glass, trinkets, small things from hands I don't ask about. Cheap, because I've little time." He opens the coat like a shop window.

events.[huk_dalekiej_armaty].scenes.[huk.t: Somewhere beyond the river there's a boom you feel in your bones before you hear it. Birds burst from the trees all at once. For a moment the wind smells of sulphur, then of grass again. The war has reminded you it exists.

events.[jarnowscy_celnicy].scenes.[jarno.t: The customs men lie by the road, the notebook open beside them at a page with a column headed "none". The wind turns the pages looking for the next one.
Darkness, legs, stones. You wake in a heap of dry seaweed behind a fence, with a bruised shoulder. The notebook lies beside you, one page torn out.
You dive into a ditch, a shot cracks over your head, and you crawl on until the first bend. The customs man shouts something after you that sounds like a promise of a lawsuit.

Two Jarnowians in grey jerkins step into the road ahead of you: one with a handgun, one with a notebook. "From the mainland? Show your hands. And your papers." Marshal Wsiewłod's letter looks like kindling here, and the handgun looks more convincing than the notebook.

events.[jarnowscy_zwiadowcy].scenes.[jar.t: The scout sinks to his knees, the marksman goes quiet halfway through a curse. Tucked in the belt of one of them you find stained maps. The area looks strangely clear on them.
You run like a dog with its tail between its legs. Behind you a bang, and a ball buries itself in the ground where you stood a moment ago. The scout laughs into his hands.

A shadow by the road moves too early. A Jarnowian scout in a grey jerkin steps out from behind a tree with the smile of a man who dislikes surprises but likes to give them. From the roof of a wrecked wagon a marksman with a handgun watches you.

events.[kieszonkowcy_w_tlumie].scenes.[k.t: The pickpockets lie between the stalls and the crowd disperses as if nothing had happened. Someone is already emptying from their pockets what they'd managed to lift themselves. The city doesn't waste time.
Something heavy hits you in the head and the world goes out. You wake in a gateway with a throbbing temple and a lighter purse. A dog is sniffing your boot.
You plunge into the crowd, knocking over a basket of fish on the way. Behind you rise the stallkeeper's shriek and two hearty curses. Pickpockets prefer not to chase where people are shouting.

In the crush by the stalls a hand slips into your purse as gently as into someone else's bed. You grab the wrist. The thief smiles, and his friend comes round behind you with a blade. "Mistake, sir. Happens to everyone."

events.[klusownicy_w_boru].scenes.[kluso.t: The poachers scuttle off with their tails between their legs and leave the sack behind. Inside are hares that nothing can hurt any more.
Two peasants with knives and a sack on their backs crawl out of the thicket. "You're the gamekeeper's man? Pity. We were hoping you'd be somebody else."
You back off quickly, and the path vanishes into the ferns. Behind you, guffaws and threats, but nobody gives chase.

events.[kolejka_do_bramy].scenes.[kolejk.t: At the gate the wagons have been queuing since dawn. The guards check every load, and one barrel makes a noise like a man. The carter grins broadly and coughs quietly. The guards hear something too, but they're buying themselves a few more groats of peace.

events.[kontrola_zwiadowcow].scenes.[kon.t: Two riders in red cloaks come out from round the bend. They slow down, then block your way, as if they'd known all along which way you'd come. The horses steam, and the mud squelches under their hooves.

events.[kowal_bez_kuzni].scenes.[kowal_b.t: The smith sits down at the crossroads and looks at his hammer as if he'd never seen it. He says nothing. After a while he fetches his apron from the ditch and heads back toward the forge.
The hammer misses your head by half an inch, but the next blow doesn't miss. You wake in a barn with aching ribs. Someone has left a bowl of soup beside you.
You run over the stones, and the hammer lands in the road where your foot just was. The smith doesn't run. He's too tired to chase someone he doesn't care about.

A broad-shouldered islander with a hammer stands at the crossroads. He's thrown his apron in the ditch, and his jerkin is ripped at the shoulder. "The hetman took my forge for the war. At least I'll have something out of it if you leave me your purse."

events.[kowal_z_mlotem].scenes.[kowal_z_.t: The smith sinks to his knees, then onto his side. The hammer rolls down the road like a wheel. The wind carries the smell of hot iron over him.
You run, and the hammer ploughs a furrow in the road where your head was a moment ago. The smith doesn't run after you. He's too big, too tired and too honest.

A broad-shouldered islander stands on the road with a hammer that could bring down walls. He's taken off his apron and put on a jerkin, but his hands still smell of iron. "I don't like doing this," he says slowly. "But I like it even less when someone jumps the queue for food ahead of me."

events.[krzykliwy_herold].scenes.[krzykl.t: On a crate a herald in a gaudy jerkin bellows: "The Emperor is well! The Emperor is watching! The Emperor announces new taxes!" People drift away looking as if they hear the same thing every day. One woman spits over her shoulder.

events.[kupiec_ostromir].scenes.[ostromi.t: A wagon with a cracked wheel stands on the verge, and beside it a plump merchant wipes the sweat off with his cap. "Ostromir's the name, I deal in cloth. When you get to Wolf's Ford, look me up – I need someone with iron at his belt as far as Stone Pass."

events.[kupiec_wedrowny].scenes.[kupiec_.t: A creaking wagon, a shaggy pony and a merchant with a belly like a barrel of sauerkraut. "Rations, bandages, arrows! Cheaper than in town – can't get any dearer than town!" The pony squints at you as if it wanted to warn you.

events.[marudery_na_drodze].scenes.[maru.t: The marauders lie in the mud. The archer has understood it was a mistake, and his last.
You leap into the forest and run until you've left their shouting behind. An arrow thuds into a tree trunk beside your head and goes on quivering for a long while.
Two ragged men in uniforms stripped of their badges block the track. A third, an archer, sits on a stump stringing his bow. "Wanderer, we've a custom here. You pay to pass, or you pass through us."

events.[mewy_nad_lodzia].scenes.[mewy_na.t: A cloud of gulls hangs behind the boat's stern, as quarrelsome as a market on Friday. One lands on the mast and eyes you like an inspector. As you leave the shore, the birds vanish one by one, until only the one on the mast is left.

events.[mewy_nad_wrakiem].scenes.[mewy_n.t: Gulls circle over a wreck lying by the shore, squabbling over something on the upper deck. They squabble with such zeal that you start to suspect they're family. When you walk off, not one of them looks up.

events.[mgla_nad_woda].scenes.[mgla_nad_.t: Fog merges water and sky into one grey wall. The helmsman slows and listens, and the oars slip into the water without a sound, as if you were sneaking. Somewhere close a buoy bell rings, or something pretending to be a buoy. The fog lifts only before dusk.

events.[noc_upiorow].scenes.[noc_atak].t.t: The air crackles with sparks till your hair stands on end. From between the trunks step two figures that might once have been men: pale, drawn long, with black holes for eyes. Skarimir's laugh breaks off halfway. "To arms!" Ragnosława shouts, and the steel goes through them as through fog.

events.[noc_upiorow].scenes.[noc_bezdroz.t: You go across country, because on the road you're more likely to meet someone, and you're in no mood for meetings. Your tunic in the school's colours sticks to your body, the mud reaches your knees, and you don't look back once. At last the palisade of Wolf's Ford rises beyond the scrub. The insignia stay at the bottom of your bundle. Nobody will ask, unless you blab.

events.[noc_upiorow].scenes.[noc_omdleni.t: The blow comes from the side. It doesn't hurt, it just chills you to the bone. Your sight goes dark, your legs give way and you go face first into the mud.

events.[noc_upiorow].scenes.[noc_swit].t.t: You wake to the cold and the wind rustling in the grass. Nothing hurts, though your shirt is stiff with dried blood. Bodies lie all around. You know whose, and you don't want to look at them. Of the whole tribute party, one is left: you. The guide isn't among the dead; he ran off like a hare and even left his bundle behind. You stuff the school's insignia into the bottom of your own, because something tells you it's better not to wear them now.

events.[noc_upiorow].scenes.[noc_zaglada.t: You can still hear things. Ragnosława goes quiet first: a shout, a spear snapping, and that's it. Skarimir tries a joke, but breaks off mid-word. Wojmir doesn't cry out at all; you only hear him drop his bundle. Then the sparks die and everything goes quiet.

events.[noc_upiorow].scenes.[noc_zmierzc.t: The day is running out, and so are Skarimir's jokes. You quicken your pace, because nobody wants to spend the night in this forest. Wojmir keeps looking over his shoulder, Ragnosława won't let go of her spear. The sky in the west turns red, and cold seeps out of the forest, though there's no wind.

events.[patrol_lodzi].scenes.[patrol_lod.t: The patrol boat drifts empty, and the waves rock it against your side until nobody's minding it. The handgun lies in the bottom, soaked.

The last thing you remember is the blow of an oar and the rush of water. You wake in the bottom of the boat, head on a coil of rope. Someone has covered you well and keeps rowing without saying where.
You slow down, then suddenly cut behind a rock. The shot rings off the water where your boat just was. The patrol doesn't chase, since its orders don't cover pursuit past the first fog.

A narrow boat comes round the headland with two Jarnowians in grey jerkins. One stands in the bow with a handgun on his shoulder, the other rows without taking his eyes off you. "Halt! Who sails without a banner?"

events.[patrol_na_goscincu].scenes.[patr.t: The soldiers lie on the highway, and their horses whinny with nobody in the saddle. Nobody will be describing your mug, today at least.
You leap the ditch and run along the edge of a field, while the soldiers curse the imperial way: long and monotonous.
On the highway two border soldiers are stopping the wagons. "Inspection!" shouts one. The other narrows his eyes and looks straight at you. You don't like that look.

events.[patrol_nocny].scenes.[patrol_noc.t: The guards lie on the cobbles next to the lantern. The flame is still smouldering, so you stamp it out with your boot. Tonight the city will have trouble working out who's watching whom.
The cudgel lands twice before you can raise an arm. You wake in the lock-up by the stove, and a guard hands your purse back, minus the charge for "lodging". They let you out in the morning.
You kick the lantern out and dive into the dark. The cudgels swish through empty air and the guards curse loudly, but they won't run after you in the dark.
Two guards with a lantern and cudgels come round the corner. One winks at the other. "No walking after curfew, sir. A fine or the irons. Choose quick, we're cold."

events.[patrol_pikinierow].scenes.[patro.t: The pikeman drops onto the road, the crossbowman slides down the slope and stays where he slid. Belts, bolts and an order nobody will carry out are left on the road.
You leap the ditch and a bolt whistles over your head like a spiteful bird. The pikeman doesn't run after you: the pike is too heavy for chases.

Two imperials in full kit stand on the road. The pikeman lowers his pike, the crossbowman on the rise takes aim. "Papers! Or pockets, if you prefer." Neither of them looks like a man who enjoys what he does.

events.[patrol_u_krateru].scenes.[patrol.t: The sergeant slumps against his ledger and falls silent. The ledger is left open at the page with your description. It isn't overly accurate.
You run down off the crater's rim over sliding glass. The sergeant yells that he'll report it, and he probably will.
Two soldiers in red are walking round the crater with spyglasses. A sergeant is writing something in a ledger. When he sees you, he slams it shut and draws his sword.

events.[patrol_zwiadowcow].scenes.[patro.t: At a bend in the forest path two scouts step out of the shadows, swords already in hand. "That's him," says one. "School of the Blade. Alive, if we can."

You throw yourself into the brush, and swords whistle where you stood a moment ago. They chase you through half the wood, until they lose your trail in a stream. You get back onto the road covered in mud to the ears and mad as a dog, but in one piece.

events.[pielgrzym].scenes.[pielgrzym_spo.t: An old pilgrim sits on a stone by the road, with a staff and a bag thinner than he is. "Where are you off to, son? The guards on these roads drink more than they guard. And when the sky starts to crackle and spark, put your iron away – a spark storm likes those who show it off." When you part, he breaks a loaf and presses half of it into your hand.

events.[pijany_zolnierz].scenes.[pijany_.t: A soldier in an imperial uniform sits on the church steps singing about a girl from Jarnowo. He breaks off to tell you: "War is the first thing you lose after dinner. And the last thing you discover." He goes back to the song. He never knew its words.

events.[pusta_lodka].scenes.[pusta_lodka.t: You pass a drifting boat with nobody in it, only a bucket, a bit of rope and a mug with the dregs of beer. The helmsman doesn't turn back. "You see more and more of those," he says. A single leaf floats in the mug, and it's hard to believe the wind blew it this far from shore.

events.[rabus_przy_brodzie].scenes.[rabu.t: The toll turns out to be void. The way across the ford is clear again, and the mud will remember footprints at most.
You hop across the stones under the water and vanish into the alders. "Toll!" someone calls after you, without conviction.
Two peasants sit by the ford with sticks and the faces of customs men. "Toll, sir. For crossing."

events.[rabusie_z_zasadzki].scenes.[rabu.t: The ambush didn't come off. What's left is the loot and the tracks in the mud.
You throw yourself into the bushes, and an arrow whistles just over your ear. You run like you've never run before.
Three men leap out of the thicket: two with cudgels and one with a bow. An ambush, and no half-hearted one either.

events.[rybacy_przy_sieci].scenes.[rybac.t: Two fishing boats are hauling a net, the fishermen shouting across the water about prices and whose turn it is. As you pass, one raises a hand in greeting, the other pretends he didn't see.

events.[rybak_z_siatka].scenes.[rybak_z_.t: A fisherman mends a net on the jetty and doesn't look up. "The fish were kind today. Take a few, I'm not afraid to share." He presses a bundle into your hand that smells of salt and smoke.

events.[rzezimieszek_w_bramie].scenes.[r.t: The cutthroat slides down the wall. The gateway is just a gateway again, and nobody at the windows saw a thing. In Ulfgród the windows never see anything.
The axe lands flat, but that's enough. You come round in the gutter feeling that someone has searched you and, while he was at it, straightened your collar.
You slip away sideways, between barrels and a fence. The axe sinks into a plank where you stood a moment ago. The cutthroat swears and ends up with a bucket of slops on his head.

A big fellow with a belly full of harbour beer and an axe slides out of a dark gateway. "Toll for passing. For the fact that nobody has whacked you here." Funny, because that's exactly what he's threatening.

events.[spotkanie_alchemik].scenes.[spot.t: A tent is pitched on a dune of glass. Inside, someone is stirring something in a cauldron and muttering to himself. "Travelling alchemist. I gather what I can and sell what I don't need. There's plenty here nobody needs." It smells of warmth and metal.

events.[spotkanie_bortnik].scenes.[spotk.t: Under a tree someone in a hood is talking and catching a swarm. It's a beekeeper, covered in bees and in a good mood. "Don't touch, don't blow, don't think about honey. Bees hear thoughts." You walk off, thinking about honey.

events.[spotkanie_drwal].scenes.[spotkan.t: By a fallen pine a woodcutter with an axe looks at you without much joy. "The Imperials were asking about you. Well, not about you, about someone who looks like you." He spits in his palm and goes back to work. "I won't say what I told them."

events.[spotkanie_handlarz_ze_szlaku].sc.t: Under a spreading oak a trader has set up shop with one mule and a pile of bags. "I don't ask where you're from, you don't ask where I got it. Business is business." He winks.

events.[spotkanie_jeniec].scenes.[spotka.t: A bound Jarnowian sits by the wagon, young, with a black eye and the look of a man who no longer has the strength to be afraid. "You ask if it hurts?" he mutters to the guard, not to you. "No. That's the worst of it." The guard looks at the sky, because it's the only place with nobody in it.

events.[spotkanie_kantynier].scenes.[spo.t: A covered wagon stands at the roadside, and on it a sutler with the face of a martyr. "Am I interrupting the war? Sorry. I'm selling what's left, because with this war nobody knows who'll be paying tomorrow." He unrolls a sheet of wares like a tablecloth.

events.[spotkanie_kowal_wedrowny].scenes.t: A fire burns by the road, and beside it a travelling smith with a portable anvil on his wagon. "I'll shoe, sharpen, mend. And if you've got something to sell, sir, I'll take that too." His hammer beats in time with his talk.

events.[spotkanie_pustelnik].scenes.[spo.t: A hermit sits on a stone and stares at the sky, as if waiting for something up there to speak. "The stars can hear. That's why people go quiet when they fall." He winks and looks up again.

events.[stare_boje].scenes.[stare_boje_s.t: In the distance sway the remains of an old line of buoys: rusted, overgrown, their chains snapped. The helmsman says they used to mark the route to Bald Rock. Now everyone sails as best they can, and nobody comes back the same way.

events.[stary_zeglarz].scenes.[stary_zeg.t: An old sailor eyes you from the deck of a moored boat. "Bald Rock? I don't go there. Anyone who's sailed close says the sky's thinner there. That when the sun sets, one side looks sharper than the other." He spits into the sea. "And the sea's a stupid invention anyway."

events.[straznik_zablakany].scenes.[stra.t: The warden slumps onto the rocks, and the visor goes dark, leaving a thin streak of smoke. Nobody reported it missing, so nobody will come looking.
The pulse hits your chest and everything goes out for a moment. You wake at the roadside with a scorched collar. The warden has gone back where it came from.
You leap off the road, and the warden walks past as if you were a stone.

A smooth figure comes out from under the rocks in armour that is neither iron nor glass. Its visor glows. "Closed ground," it says without stopping, even though you're standing in the middle of the road. It keeps heading straight for you anyway.

events.[strzelec_z_dachu].scenes.[strzel.t: The marksman slides off the roof along with some shingles and sits in the grass, out cold. A scout lies beside him. At the fork the wind takes over giving orders again.
The ball hits your shoulder and the world spins. You wake under the shed, bandaged by someone who left no name. The handgun lies beside you with no powder in it.
You throw yourself behind the shed, and the ball clangs off a barrel. The marksman swears, since he reloads too slowly. You roll into a ditch and go on under cover of the fence.
A gun barrel flashes on the roof of a shed at the fork. A handgun is aimed straight at you. "Halt! By order of the hetman!" shouts someone who hasn't yet decided whether that's true.

events.[studnia_przy_targu].scenes.[stud.t: Women crowd around the well in the market. One speaks in a lowered voice: "They say there's something in the water that lets you drop in a coin and make a wish. They just don't say who grants it." Someone snorts with laughter and walks off with a bucket.

events.[szabrownicy_na_plazy].scenes.[sz.t: The looters lie on the sand, and the surf washes the tar off their hands. The sacks stay. The gulls move in to inspect.
You wake on the sand, collar wet, with seaweed on your forehead. The surf drew back exactly far enough that you didn't drown.
You dodge between the boat's ribs and vanish behind a dune. The axe sinks into the sand. Nobody follows, since the sacks won't carry themselves.

On the beach, among the broken ribs of a boat, two men with sacks look up. One pulls out an axe with the face of a man who knows what other people's timber is worth. "This is our shore. Pay the toll or go another way."

events.[szabrownicy_przy_drodze].scenes..t: The looters lie in the grass and take nothing any more. Their sacks have spilled across the road: cups, buttons, one boot without its pair. Everything left of people who won't be coming back.
You jump the ditch and run until you can't hear their cursing. The looters don't chase you. They have work.

Two skinny shadows with sacks crawl out of the ditch. One waves a knife like a little flag. "Hey, you! Leave what you've got and move along, we're working here." The work is taking from the fallen, and from the living too, if they don't defend themselves.

events.[sztorm_na_horyzoncie].scenes.[sz.t: A dark blue wall is rising on the horizon, and the water in front of it goes smooth as glass. The helmsman swears through his teeth and holds the course as best he can. The storm passes you by on one side, as if it preferred a look from afar to the real thing. It's an hour before you stop clenching the gunwale.

events.[utopiec_w_rowie].scenes.[utopiec.t: The drowner sinks into the slime without a word. The water ripples and settles, as if nothing had happened.
You run over the stones, and behind your back something splashes that would rather you'd stayed.
Water stands in the ditch by the road, black as pitch. Something sticks out of it and waves at you with a hand that isn't human.

events.[wdowa_na_molo].scenes.[wdowa_na_.t: A woman in a black shawl sits at the end of the pier, looking out to sea. "My husband sailed with the fleet. Don't tell me he'll be back, sir. Everybody says that, and then they go quiet." She doesn't wait for an answer.

events.[weszyciel_na_rynku].scenes.[wesz.t: The informer lies in the shade of a stall with the needle in his hand. Nobody asks who killed him. In this city everyone has something worse on their conscience than a sideways glance.
The needle goes into your shoulder and your whole side goes numb. You come to against a wall, with a whisper still in your ears: "The Emperor remembers."
You dive into a side alley and turn three times in twenty paces. The informer loses you by the church, because people keep getting underfoot here.

A man in a grey cloak has been following you for three stalls. You stop, so does he. He pulls a needle from inside his coat as long as a finger. "Imperial enquiry, sir. Where are you from?" The answer doesn't matter here.

events.[wiatr_od_morza].scenes.[wiatr_od.t: A wind comes off the sea, smelling of salt and something metallic. For a moment you can taste a coin on your tongue. Then the wind drops, as if it had meant to tell you something and thought better of it.

events.[wilki].scenes.[wilki_po_walce].t.t: You wipe the gore off your blade and listen. The forest is silent. You walk on, glancing over your shoulder every few steps.

events.[wilki].scenes.[wilki_ucieczka].t.t: You scramble up onto a fallen trunk and wave your iron about till the wolves lose interest. They slink off into the forest, and you hear their howling for a long while after.

events.[wilki].scenes.[wilki_wycie].text.t: Two wolves come out of the undergrowth. Thin, fangs bared – hunger has driven them out of the forest by day. They don't growl. They just come at you.

events.[wozy_z_frontu].scenes.[wozy_z_fr.t: Wagons from the front roll through the city, filthy with mud and covered with tarpaulins, from under which something sticks out here and there. Nobody looks. Kids run after the first wagon, and an old market woman covers her face with her apron.

events.[wozy_z_lodzi].scenes.[wozy_z_lod.t: Wagons roll along the road with boats on their flatbeds: new, straight from the carpenters, still sticky with tar. The carters swear at every bump. There are no markings on the wagons. Everyone knows nobody has come back yet from any of these boats.

events.[zebrak_na_moscie].scenes.[zebrak.t: A beggar sits on the bridge staring into the river as if waiting for an answer. "Spare a groat, sir, and I'll tell you who fell in the water yesterday." Instead of a groat you give him a look. He laughs. "Good. Nobody. That was a good answer."

events.[zmije_w_trawie].scenes.[zmije_w_.t: The last viper coils up and vanishes. The path is a path again, not a snake pit.
You jump off the road and give the clump a wide berth. The vipers don't hold it against you.
The grass on both sides of the road hisses like a market woman. A viper slithers out from under a stone, then another. They've come out for the sun.

locations.[bagna_szarej_wody].spots.[gro.t: The log causeway rots in silence, and the bog beneath it gurgles like a belly after bad porridge. In the middle of it lies a boot. Just the one, with no owner. Bone dry, which out here is more frightening than if it weren't there at all.

locations.[bagna_szarej_wody].spots.[top.t: The drowner slumps into the slime, and the wisp goes out with a quiet hiss. The bog pool falls silent. Not for long, but long enough to get out with dry feet.
You wake in the bog, filthy to the elbows, with an empty head and a green mark on your neck. Someone pulled you out at the last moment. Who, nobody knows.
You run from tussock to tussock, and behind you the water splashes and something whispers your name. No, it isn't the wind.
The water in the bog pool stands black as pitch, and even the mosquitoes keep away. Something lies on the bank and doesn't move. Beside it, something green rises out of the water.

locations.[bagna_szarej_wody].spots.[wed.t: The angler sits with his rod over something that, with goodwill, you might call water. "A drowner ate all the fish. But I keep fishing, because if I catch him, I'll give him a piece of my mind. Last time I pulled out his boot. His, I think."
"It's you. The fish don't bite, the drowner doesn't bite, nothing bites. But I sit."
"You'll scare off my fish, if there's any left. Go and stand further off, over there, where the mud's deeper."
The angler stares at his float. The float twitches, and for the first time since morning he smiles.

locations.[bor_klusownikow].spots.[oboz_.t: The marauders lie in the brush, and their fire still smells of roast squirrel. You leave the uniforms be, because they stink.
You came to in the branches, with a sore head and a lighter purse. The marauders moved on and left you two apple cores. Generous bastards.
You burst out of the bushes, with curses and stones flying after you.
Four ragged men in what's left of imperial coats sit in the thicket. Deserters, hungry and mean. The one with a knife between his teeth sees you and gets up.

locations.[bor_klusownikow].spots.[polan.t: The wood is thick and quiet, and in the quiet all you hear is the creak of snares. Thin wires wind between the ferns, and under a beech someone has laid out knife blades in an arrow. The arrow says it plain: turn back while you've still got legs.

locations.[bor_klusownikow].spots.[sojka.t: Under an oak sits a beanpole in a moth-eaten coat, whistling at the jays. The jays couldn't care less. "I was a woodsman once. Now I just keep out of the leshy's way, because he's master here. I don't bother him, he doesn't lead me astray. And you, stranger, don't whistle in the woods after dark."
"You're back. The birds wake me up, and I can't stand them. But at least you don't whistle."
The jay-whistler squints at you with pity. "There's nothing here but snares and my foul temper. Turn back while you've still got legs."
The jay-whistler whistles at the jays, and the jays don't give a damn. "One more day of this and I'll start flapping my wings myself."

locations.[cmentarz_lodzi].spots.[lodzie.t: Hundreds of boats lie keel-up on the sand, each with a date and a name carved into its side. The wind plays in their empty bellies.
At night the boats on the sand creak as if somebody inside were turning over onto the other side.
The old man laying seaweed along a gunwale raises his head. "You the one who runs errands?" He doesn't wait for an answer. He goes on laying seaweed.
At dusk the shadows of the boats stretch out across the sand.

locations.[cmentarz_lodzi].spots.[szabro.t: The looters lie beside their own wheelbarrow, and the side with the name goes back where it belongs, though somebody will have to nail it on.
You wake under an upturned boat, head ringing, a stranger's plank under your back. Someone covered you with seaweed, like the dead. Or like the wounded.
You run down the sand between the boats, the looters' shouting carrying over the empty beach. The axe sinks into a gunwale right where your head was a moment ago. The boat has no comment.

Two looters are stripping the side off a boat with a name nobody bears any more and throwing the planks into a wheelbarrow. As you come closer, one raises an axe. "You saw nothing here. Wood belongs to nobody."

locations.[cmentarz_zbiorowy].hint.t: smoke and the smell of lime east of the walls, a day's walk

locations.[cmentarz_zbiorowy].spots.[bly.t: Between the mounds, where the gravedigger's spade hasn't reached yet, something glints in the freshly turned earth. It's a little pouch pushed down into the grave, as if someone couldn't decide whether to hide it or give it to the dead. Inside are herbs and some small coin.
The hole where the pouch was has been filled in. Nobody's looking for anything here now, not even you.

locations.[cmentarz_zbiorowy].spots.[gra.t: The gravedigger digs in silence, as if there were nobody he had anything to say to. When he glances at you, he measures you the way you'd measure a pit.
At night the graveyard can get loud. It isn't the dead making the noise, but the living, who come here looking for what they haven't the nerve for by day.
The gravedigger leans on his spade. "I've heard about you. They say where you go, there's more work." He spits, without malice. "For me that means more bread."
At dusk the lime shows white in the earth like snow in drifts. The gravedigger lights a lamp and sets it by the pit so nobody falls in.

locations.[cmentarz_zbiorowy].spots.[wla.t: The thieves lie among the mounds, and the gravedigger watches from afar, nodding as if he'd waited for this for weeks. Something still glints in the ground.
You wake in a ditch with mud in your mouth. The gravedigger doesn't ask what happened. He only asks if you want a swig of water.
You vault a mound and run between the crosses. Behind you curses and one clang of a spade on stone.
At a fresh mound two thieves are rooting in the earth and a third stands watch with a club. He spots you before you can back off. "What are you here for? This is our workplace!"

locations.[dom_ciszy].hint.t: a grey temple behind the market square that nobody mentions out loud

locations.[dom_ciszy].spots.[krypta_cisz.t: The crypt is cold and quiet; the noise stays at the gate. The nuns sweep the floor in a rhythm nobody calls prayer.
At night you can hear breathing in the crypt. Hard to say whose. Nobody asks.
The nuns look up when you come in. One whispers to another, "That's him." The other says, "I know." And they go back to work.
The nuns light the candles one by one, in an order that matters only to them.

locations.[dom_czarnego_szkla].hint.t: a smooth, windowless house on the slope behind the Shipyard, where nobody lives

locations.[dom_czarnego_szkla].spots.[cz.t: The wall is dark and smooth, as if it had never spoken. The Blade at your belt goes silent.

locations.[dom_czarnego_szkla].spots.[wn.t: By day the light comes into the house only through the door, and bounces about the walls until the inside seems bigger than the outside. The floor is warm underfoot.
The house is so quiet at night you can hear your own pulse. The glass trembles slightly, as if waiting to see whether someone will ring it with iron.
As you enter, the glass brightens for a moment, as if it knew you from stories. It says nothing. Islanders say the house likes people who clean up after themselves.
At dusk the walls begin to glow from within with a pale, milky light. The shadow of your Blade stretches half a step too far.

locations.[gluszec].spots.[chlopiec].sce.t: A boy in a shirt too big for him is dragging a goat on a rope, the goat is dragging him, and the goat is winning. "You're the one from over the pass, sir? Granny says strigas come from over the pass and you mustn't look them in the eye. I look. Yours are normal. Just dirty."
"Oh, it's you again, sir. Don't put anything down near her. Yesterday she ate the reeve's notice off the fence. If he asks, you saw nothing."

The boy gives you a pitying look. "Got nothing to do, sir? Well, I have. I'm minding the goat. Mum says if she eats one more thing, she'll sell me to the Emperor and keep the goat, because the goat gives milk."
"No time, the goat!" The boy goes past on his belly through the mud, the rope in his fist. The goat heads for the neighbour's cabbages and doesn't even look back.

locations.[gluszec].spots.[cmentarz].sce.t: The graveyard is bigger than the village and a lot quieter. The crosses lean every which way, as if they'd been shoving each other for room. Some graves have fresh herbs on them, others nothing, and on one lie three stones laid out in a star. Nobody will tell you who put them there. Better not to ask, so you don't wake anything. By day the stones are dead and cold. The old folk say they only come alive after dark.

locations.[gluszec].spots.[pijak].scenes.t: The drunk by the fence opens one eye and slurs. "There was a wedding. The smith's wife's girl. Three days I drank on tick, and I'm still drinking, because the innkeeper thinks it's still the wedding. Don't tell him, stranger, or he'll beat me to death."
"You again? I dream about my debts, and when I dream about them, they grow like bread dough. Go easy on the tick, stranger."
The drunk waves a hand as if swatting a talking fly. "I've got my own business, dawn to dawn. A man who drinks has no time for other people's affairs."
The drunk rolls over by the fence. "The wedding's still on. Come back when it's over." And he's asleep mid-sentence.

locations.[gluszec].spots.[piwnica].scen.t: Behind the barrels of sauerkraut there's a little door the innkeeper says isn't there. Behind it is a cramped cubby with a straw pallet, two waterskins and a hole in the wall you can see the yard through. It stinks like a kennel.

locations.[gluszec].spots.[stara_baba].s.t: An old woman on a bench outside her hut is shelling peas into a pot, and she doesn't stop as you come up. "Got salt in your pocket, young one? No? Then you're a fool. There's a night-hag walks here of a night and sits on the chest of anyone who sleeps without salt. In my day everyone carried some."
"You again. I don't sleep, because I'm old. What's your excuse? Bad conscience?"
The old woman doesn't even look up. "I'll tell you nothing, because I know nothing, and what I knew I've forgotten. The peas won't shell themselves."
"Keep salt in your pocket, I said." The old woman goes on shelling. She's said her piece.

locations.[gluszec].visitors.[szept_o_cm.t: By the well the children whisper that the stones in the graveyard glow after dark and talk in a voice they haven't got. The grown-ups spit and change the subject. If you want to listen, go there at night.

locations.[jar_dezerterow].hint.t: smoke in a deep ravine, four days from camp

locations.[jar_dezerterow].spots.[oboz_d.t: A few huts, a cauldron and wooden bunks stand under the rock overhang in the ravine. Deserters in patched jackets play dice for other people's boots. An Imperial uniform and a Jarnowian jacket hang on the same line, as if the war were nothing but laundry here.
At night the ravine is quiet as a grave. The watch is the boy with the stick, who falls asleep every second sentence, and nobody punishes him for it.

Talk dies down around the fire. Somebody whispers your name like a rumour, and one of the deserters glances at the blade at your belt. "You're the one sorting things out for the captain?" he asks. "Then sit down. Nobody here settles accounts with anybody, except hunger."

The huts stand empty, somebody has taken the cauldron, and a single jacket hangs on the line, not worth the trouble of carrying. The water in the ravine rushes on as before. Only the boy with the stick is gone, and now nobody sleeps on watch here.
At dusk the campfires light up one after another. Somebody sings a song whose words everybody gets wrong, and yet everybody knows the tune.

locations.[jar_dezerterow].spots.[pogon].t: The pikeman lowers his pike and sits on a rock as if somebody had just lifted a whole regiment off his back. The looters lie next to him. All you can hear in the ravine is water again.
You wake in a hut, under a blanket, with a dressing on your head. The deserters ask no questions. One hands you a bowl of hot water and looks away.
You climb the bank while the pikeman curses below. The looters don't follow: they know that whoever runs always drops something.

A pursuit comes down from the top of the ravine: an Imperial pikeman with two looters, who want to hunt something down so as not to go back empty-handed. They don't ask who you are. They only ask whether you have anything worth taking.

locations.[jar_dezerterow].spots.[skrytk.t: The cache stands empty. Handprints in the dust remain, and the smell of old broadcloth.
Behind a stone at the mouth of the ravine somebody has built a cache: tight, dry, with a bit of cord for a handle. Inside lie things the deserters took from the army and never dared to sell.

locations.[kamieniolom].spots.[kamieniar.t: The stonemason swings his hammer at a boulder as if he doesn't care whether it cracks. "I carve gravestones. In Głuszec it's the only work that never runs out. People die, the stone stays, and I take a groat a letter, so short names are the ruin of me."
"You again. The stone doesn't sleep, I don't sleep, so we can stay up together. Just don't tell me how many letters are in your name."
"This is a stone for breaking, and I'm the one breaking it. Stand back, a chip doesn't pick who it hits."
The stonemason brings his hammer down on the boulder so the sparks fly at your feet. The conversation's over.

locations.[kamieniolom].spots.[sztolnia].t: The tunnel gapes in the hillside like a black mouth. The props are blackened with damp, and on one of them hangs a lamp that hasn't seen tallow or oil in a long while. Water drips from the depths, and now and then something scrabbles.

locations.[kapliczka_rozstaje].hint.t: a bell carried on the wind

locations.[kapliczka_rozstaje].spots.[ka.t: The shrine is small and crooked, and the little saint inside has one eye and the face of a man with toothache. Offerings lie before him: an ear of wheat, a horseshoe and a candle stub with clear teeth marks in it.

locations.[kapliczka_rozstaje].spots.[pu.t: The hermit looks like a man who lost his faith in people and found it in mushrooms. "Don't disturb me. I'm praying against drowners, so they don't crawl out of the marsh. Or I'm counting how many have crawled out already. I never know which of the two I'm doing."
"You again. I sleep fine, only with my eyes open. That way I see what I'm dreaming."
"I've got my work: doing nothing, with all my heart. Don't get in the way of my difficult quest."
The hermit lays mushrooms out in rows and counts them in a whisper. When you interrupt him, he starts again from the beginning, without a grudge.

locations.[koszary].hint.t: grey walls with a red banner, a day's walk north of the market square

locations.[koszary].spots.[kwatermistrz].t: The patrol lies in a row as if for roll call. The commander stares at the sky, surprised that he's still breathing. The paper with your description slips from his hand and lands in a puddle.
You come to on a bench in the town lockup. Towards morning someone opens the door, casually, and points you to the exit. You don't ask why.
You run down an alley, boots thudding behind you. At the junction the patrol stops: their orders don't reach past the corner.

A town patrol stops you at the barracks gate. The commander looks from you to the paper in his hand and back at you, as if comparing two portraits he likes equally little. The guards close in slowly, almost elegantly.

locations.[koszary].spots.[plac_apelowy].t: The recruits are learning a march that has little to do with marching. The sergeant shouts at them so keenly they almost stop being afraid.
At night from the barracks come snoring, coughing and the whisper of a lad praying that tomorrow nobody calls out his name.
Recruits drill on the parade ground in civilian boots. The sergeant sizes you up and mutters, "We could use you. Shame you're not ours." It sounds like a compliment, and probably is one.
At dusk the barracks shut their gates. The guards count each other to be sure nobody has deserted.

locations.[koszary].spots.[skrzynia_kwat.t: Against the wall, behind the sacks of barley, stands a chest with brass fittings. Someone has already broken the lock and didn't bother with what's inside: dressings, a herbal draught and a handful of groats left over from a divided payroll.
The chest stands open. All that's left is sawdust and a receipt nobody wants.

locations.[koszary].spots.[szabrownicy_w.t: Both lie among the crates. The sacks stay, because nobody knows whose they are, and you don't want to be next in line for questions.
You wake among the crates with a lump on your head. The storehouse is empty and so are the looters, so nobody will report anything.
You jump out of the window. Behind you there's smashing glass and cursing, as if you were the one wrecking their storehouse.

Behind the barracks stands a storehouse with supposedly nothing in it. Two men are standing in it all the same, stuffing sacks with what isn't there. They size you up, and each waits for the other to reach for a cudgel first.

locations.[krater_gwiazdy].spots.[krater.t: The crater has the shape of a hand that opened its fingers for a moment. At the bottom lies a lump of iron as big as a barrel. From the edge you can see the glass darken the closer it gets to the middle.

The air over the crater thickens, your hair stands on end, and something crackles quietly in your ears like fat in a pan. Blue sparks shoot up from the bottom and don't go out, even when you hold your hand to them. The sky starts to spark.

locations.[krater_gwiazdy].spots.[pustel.t: A man sits on the edge of the crater with his legs dangling over and counts the sparks on his fingers. "Forty-two. Always forty-two. Too many for chance, too few for a plan. I've got the answer, only the devil knows what the question was."
"Oh, it's you again. I'm waiting for them to make up their minds. I've got time, so have they, only they've got more of it."
"I've got my work: counting. Forty-two, same as always."
The man scratches his shoulder and doesn't stop counting. As you turn away, he mutters "forty-three" and looks as if he has a bone to pick with his own mouth.

locations.[kuznie].spots.[zar_paleniska].t: The hearth roars and the smiths work to a rhythm you can feel in your chest. Sparks fall on the packed earth like tiny stars.
At night the hearth barely glows.
An apprentice hands you a mug of cold water without asking what for. "The smith says you know how to listen, sir," he whispers, and vanishes behind the bellows.
At dusk the smiths bank the hearths and wash their faces in the troughs, and red shadows are left on the walls.

locations.[lesniczowka].hint.t: a chimney deep in the forest, two days' walk east

locations.[lesniczowka].spots.[gniewosz].t: By a woodpile stands a skinny boy with an axe bigger than he is. "I'm Gniewosz. The forester says I've a gift for trees. The trees say I don't." He goes on chopping without looking.
Gniewosz wipes his brow with his sleeve. "Two days' walk from the Ford, and folk turn up like it's a tavern. Yesterday one asked for beer. We've got sour rye soup and a dog."
"The forester told me to count the roe deer. I got to four, and lost count at the fifth, because it ran off." The boy nods as if that explains everything.
Gniewosz nods to you and doesn't stop chopping. "Mind the path on your way back. Something's been howling lately, but maybe that was the forester singing."

locations.[lesniczowka].spots.[pies].sce.t: The forester's big dog raises its head, looks you over and goes back to its nap. Someone shouts from behind the hut: "Burek! Don't bark at folk with swords!" Burek yawns. A sword doesn't count for much with him.
Burek growls once, short, to show he remembers you. From the hut: "That wanderer again? Get him out of here, he'll upset my dog!"
The dog doesn't even blink. He couldn't care less about anything that isn't a bone.

locations.[lesniczowka].spots.[schowek]..t: Someone buried a box under a broken oak at the edge of the glade, and did it badly, because the lid sticks a hand's breadth out of the ground. Inside are herbs in little pouches, a roll of clean linen and a handful of coins. Poacher's or forester's, who knows, and best not to wonder.
The box stands open and empty. All that's left inside is sawdust and one ant.

locations.[lesniczowka].spots.[sidla].sc.t: Both of them lie in the leaves. You take the snares down one by one and toss them on the fire. The forester will ask questions anyway, but at least there'll be something to ask about.
You wake under a bush with a lump the size of an egg. The poachers have packed up camp. The snares stayed, because they know they'll be back.
You back away down the path. Behind you there's laughter, and something heavy crashes into the bushes next to you. You don't check what.

In the copse behind the forester's hut someone has strung snares across half the forest. By a fire two peasants in rags are skinning something that not long ago belonged to the forester. At the sight of you one reaches for his knife, the other for what's left of the hare.

locations.[loch_pod_palacem].spots.[komn.t: The Core Chamber is silent. The pillar stands dark and the cables hang like ropes after a long voyage. No one gives orders here any more.

The Steward kneels as if to sign one last time. The mask cracks along a single tube and the light that flowed through it goes out. Around the Core the cables lose their warmth one by one. The pillar doesn't die. It is left without an owner, like a house after a fire in which the table still stands.

The clause closes over you like a lid. You wake in the corridor in front of the iron door. The Steward doesn't pursue. He doesn't have to: he knows where you are, because you're the only contracting party still walking around.

The iron door opens by itself, as if you were on its list. In the chamber stands the Core: a pillar of copper and glass, tall as a tower, tangled in cables that pulse with warm light. Beside it, hands folded, waits the Steward. His mask of copper tubes has no expression, but his voice does.

locations.[loch_pod_palacem].spots.[kust.t: The Keeper falls among the cables and the lantern rolls across the floor. For a moment sparks leap along the wires like startled birds, then everything goes quiet and the chamber gets darker.
A spark, a whip of cable, darkness. You wake in the corridor smelling of singed hair. The Keeper is straightening his wires and doesn't look your way.
In the round chamber the cables hang lifeless. The Keeper's lantern sits where it rolled, snuffed out, and no one is straightening the wires.
You jump back as a cable spits a spark right by your face. The Keeper doesn't move. This is his place, and you are a guest without leave.

In a round chamber all the cables from the palace come together, thick, copper, wrapped in rags and tar. A thin figure with a lantern and pliers is busy among them, stroking the wires like horses. "Don't touch," he says without turning his head. "That's all that keeps them alive. Them, not us."

locations.[loch_pod_palacem].spots.[nies.t: The Sleepless slumps onto the stone and closes his eyes for the first time in years. He looks like a man who has finally been given leave. You don't wake him.
His gaze holds you like a paw. When the last blow lands nothing hurts any more, only the cold. You wake in the corridor. The Sleepless is back against the wall, staring at a single point again.
The cell is quiet. The Sleepless lies against the wall with his eyes shut, breathing evenly, like someone who is truly sleeping after years.
You back out of the cell, and his gaze follows you all the way to the corner. No steps chase you. The eyes do.

This corridor ends in a small cell with no bed in it. A gaunt man sits against the wall, his eyes not blinking for twenty years. This is the Sleepless: the first who agreed to guard the Core, and got insomnia instead of pay. He rises without hurry. "Have you come to free me or kill me? To me it's the same service."

locations.[loch_pod_palacem].spots.[stra.t: The warden slumps onto the threshold, his armour clanks once against the slab and falls quiet. The helmet rolls across the stone to the wall. For the first time in years no one is guarding the entrance, and he seems never to have known he was free to leave.
The spear lands once, and a second blow isn't needed. You wake on the stairs, dragged to where the threshold ends. The warden is back in his place. His place is all he has.
The threshold is empty. The grooved slab waits for steps that will never come, and the armour lies where it fell.
You back away up the stairs. The warden doesn't follow: the threshold is his border and holds him tighter than any chain.

At the bottom of the stairs the corridor narrows to a threshold of stone slab, worn with grooves from boots. The Warden of the Threshold has stood here since the day the pact was sealed. His armour is perfectly clean, his face perfectly empty. "No entry without an invitation," he says, as if reading from a card. The Emperor is dead, but an order outlives an emperor.

locations.[loch_pod_palacem].spots.[szep.t: The Whisperer falls silent mid-sentence. The gallery is left with an echo that goes on repeating your name for a while, until it forgets whom it was calling.
The whisper gets into your head like water into a boat, and suddenly you don't know what you came here for. You wake at the mouth of the gallery, your own voice still ringing in your ears.
The gallery is silent. The shadow of a hood still slides along the wall, though no one wears it any more, and only now and then does the echo repeat a scrap of a sentence.
You plug your ears and run, but the whisper follows you all the way to the stairs, repeating things you never told anyone.

You can hear a quiet conversation in the stone gallery, and there is nobody there to hold it. Only after a moment do you see a hooded man, pale as a candle, talking to the wall. He turns to you and the whisper changes the subject: now it's about you, in your own words, from a week ago.

locations.[loch_pod_palacem].spots.[wejs.t: The stairs go down deeper than the palace foundations should allow. The walls sweat cold, and copper cables as thick as an arm run along the ceiling. Someone knew that something that shouldn't get out had to be kept here. Someone else knew it would pay off.
The corridor knows your step by now. On one side a guardroom by the threshold, on the other a cable lock, and somewhere in the depths something purrs like a cat the size of a barn.
Three guards lie behind you, and deeper in, where the cables thicken like roots, someone has not slept for many years. You don't hear his steps. You feel them in the floor.
Past the cell of the Sleepless the corridor ends at an iron door, copper light seeping through its cracks. The rest of the dungeon is quiet now. One place is left, the one everything else led to.

locations.[lysa_skala].hint.t: a lone rock with a glow at the edge of the map, four days by boat, where nobody sails

locations.[lysa_skala].spots.[brama].sce.t: The gate stands silent. Whatever you had to decide about it, you've already decided.

The guards on the approach turn their visors toward you, but don't move from their places. Their boundary ends at the foot of the rock. The crack with the vortex in it is further on, where none of them ever goes.

locations.[lysa_skala].spots.[podejscie].t: The rock rises from the sea like a tooth, wind-smoothed and cracked in one place, where a light seeps out in a colour the rainbow doesn't have.
At night the rock is the only bright spot on the sea. The Blade at your belt rings thinly, as if you were carrying a lantern.
The hetman's boat is moored at the jetty, and beside it stands a helmsman staring at the ground. "You're on your own from here," he says. He doesn't ask what for.
At dusk the light in the crack grows stronger and gives off a faint note, like a string nobody is plucking.

locations.[lysa_skala].spots.[schowek_st.t: The cache is open and empty, and the lid shuts quietly, as if offended.
In a hollow of the rock sits a cache made of something that is neither iron nor glass. The lid gives way when the Blade rings. Inside lie things the guards left because they couldn't take them along.

locations.[lysa_skala].spots.[straz_bram.t: The guards slump onto the stone without a cry. The visors go dark one after the other, and the rock is just a rock again, with one odd crack in it.
The pulse knocks the breath out of you, then your sight. You wake on the jetty with a smell of scorching in your hair. The guards are back at their posts.
You scramble down the rocks, and behind you something cracks and leaves black marks on the stone. The guards don't run after you; their boundary ends at the foot of the approach.
Two guards in smooth armour stand on the approach. Their visors glow with the same light as the crack in the rock. "Closed ground," one says, in a voice with no reason to sound human.

locations.[menhiry].spots.[kamieniarka]..t: An old woman is tucking moss around one of the standing stones as if she were tucking a grandchild in under a feather bed. "They remember. They remember everything. Only people forget, because it's easier that way. Don't go waking trouble, young one."
"Oh, it's you again. The stones don't sleep, so neither do I. Mind you don't come too close at night."
"The standing stones have their own business. And I've got them all waiting their turn."
The old woman wipes another stone down with moss and gives it a reproachful look. It keeps quiet, the way stones do.

locations.[menhiry].spots.[krag].scenes..t: Twelve stones stand in a ring, each taller than a man, each with one side smooth as a mirror. You lay your hand on one and the stone is warm as a cow's flank, and a murmur swells in your ears, as if many voices were talking at once so quietly that none of them says anything.

locations.[oboz_cesarski_przedni].hint.t: red banners beyond the hills, half a day's march

locations.[oboz_cesarski_przedni].spots..t: The field kitchen is three cauldrons, one table and a cook with the face of a martyr. The soup is supposedly pea, but tastes like dishwater.
At night the kitchen is quiet, only the coals crackle in the fire pit. Someone is secretly scraping the bottom of the cauldron, and when he sees you, he pretends to be cleaning.

The cook presses a ladle into your hand. "So you're the one running errands for the captain? Tell him we're running low on porridge, and the soldiers still have an appetite." He says it as if you could do something about it.
At dusk the soldiers line up with their bowls. The cook ladles like a judge, without mercy and without exceptions.
The lieutenant's tent is clean and orderly like the conscience of a man who never had anything to hide. Meaning like the conscience of someone who likes to think so about himself.

locations.[oboz_hetmana].hint.t: campfire smoke over the hill by the bay, a day's walk from the Shipyard

locations.[oboz_hetmana].spots.[patrol_p.t: The patrol lies by the palisade, and the sentry on the tower pretends he saw nothing.
You wake by the well with ice-cold water on your face. Somebody doused you, somebody dragged you off, and nobody said why.
You double back between the tents, and a shot from the palisade clangs off a cauldron. The scout doesn't chase you: he knows the edge of the camp better than his own name.

A patrol that doesn't know you by sight stops you at the palisade. The scout circles in from the side while the marksman climbs onto the walkway. "Stranger with no colours. The hetman doesn't like those who turn up uninvited."

locations.[oboz_hetmana].spots.[plac_obo.t: On the camp square soldiers clean their handguns, talk under their breath and look at you the way you look at weather you can't trust.
At night the camp breathes in snoring, coughing and the whispers of sentries counting the hours to the changeover.
The camp sergeant nods and points you to a free spot by the fire. "The hetman's heard of you," he says without enthusiasm. From an islander, that's practically a hug.
At dusk fires are lit on the square, with cauldrons of fish soup hung over them. Half the island stinks of it.

locations.[oboz_hetmana].spots.[skrzynka.t: Behind the supply tent stands a crate covered with a horse blanket. Under it, between a spare blanket and a whetstone, lie some rotgut and a stock of dressings. Somebody remembers it's there, just not today, apparently.
The crate stands empty. On the bottom lie a horse blanket and the mark of a bottle.

locations.[oboz_jarnowian_przedni].hint.t: campfires across the river, two days from camp

locations.[oboz_jarnowian_przedni].spots.t: A wicker basket sits in the shallows by the ford, tied to a stake so the current won't take it. Inside, under a wet rag, you find rotgut in a skin, dressings and a few coins. Somebody here is fishing for more than fish.
The basket sits by its stake, empty. The water flows around it as if nothing had happened.

The island forge smells of oil, powder and the sharp, foreign tang of a metal you don't know. The smith doesn't look up, but his silence has something of an invitation to talk about it. Or to a brawl.
A few islanders in blue jackets sit by the fire. They talk in their own tongue and laugh at something you don't understand, which is probably you.
At night the islanders polish their handgun barrels in silence.
The Jarnowians around the fire stop singing when they see you. One raises his mug at you. "So you're the one wrecking our plans, wanderer?" He says it without anger, almost with respect.
At dusk the Jarnowians sing. You can't make out the words, but they're off-key just like ours.
Both lie in the reeds. You pick your arrows up off the ground, since you're running low on your own.
You wake in the reeds with a runny nose and empty pockets. The scouts are gone, like everybody else around here.
You dive behind a fallen tree, then run for the reeds. Arrows keep falling behind you all the way to the bank and a little past it.
Two islanders in hides, arrows already out, patrol the bank by the ford. When they spot you they don't shout or ask questions. They just draw their bows, because it's quicker.

locations.[oboz_wronia].spots.[ognisko]..t: The fire smokes lazily, a pot hangs over it, and nobody knows what is in it. The soldiers throw dice for who eats and who pays for the kindling.

New men sit by the wagons, in jackets with faded patches. Thirty-two lads from the ravine. Nobody asks them anything, nobody says good day, but someone moves the cauldron closer. A sergeant with no patch makes sure the hardtack is shared out evenly.

The scouts came back from the ravine empty-handed. Lean-tos empty, ash cold, not a trace of the thirty men. The captain crosses something out in his notebook. "So they weren't there," he says and goes to sleep. By the fire someone raises a mug without saying what for.

This morning a unit from the ravine came through. Tied together on one rope, thirty-two of them, a grey-haired sergeant in front. They looked at no one. The captain ordered them taken to the Hill, and by the fire nobody gambles and nobody says what he thinks about it. They paid out the wages for it, though. Today of all days.
At night the fire smoulders down to embers, and those who can't sleep sit around it. They talk in whispers, so the sentry doesn't turn them into a report.

Someone by the fire calls over: "So you're the one doing the jobs off the board?" Then silence, but the kind where everyone looks at you with curiosity. Someone points you to a spot on a stump: the quietest promotion in the world.

For the first time in a month someone is laughing by the fire. The Jarnowians walked up the Old Road to the fort, all hundred of them, straight into the imperial crossbows. Forty didn't get up. "They must've been drunk," someone says. "Or someone sold them good news," says another, and everyone laughs, because it's a good joke. You take a mug and say nothing.

Nobody's gambling tonight. The powder wagon train burned at the crossing, three wagons and their carters, and the Jarnowians were waiting in the reeds like men who'd been sent a letter with the date on it. Someone asks how they knew. Nobody answers, but everyone has started watching who sits down next to them. And there's no powder left to shoot with anyway.

Strange news has come from across the river. The Jarnowians fired a volley and half their handguns just coughed. Our lot were over the ford before they could reload. "Their powder was wet," says the carter. "Everything's wet on the islands," says another, and that's the end of that.
At dusk it gets crowded by the wagons. Someone wails an old song, someone else asks him to stop, and both wishes come true at once.

locations.[oboz_wronia].visitors.[kapita.t: A messenger in a stained jacket stops in front of you and salutes his own way, meaning he slouches a little. "The captain asks you to the command tent. Says it can't wait, but all his business waits, so I don't know what that means."

locations.[oboz_wronia].visitors.[stary_.t: Someone sits on a barrel sharpening a knife on a stone, slowly, with feeling. You recognise the old soldier from the Last Watchtower. "War again. A man thinks he's seen it all, and here you go, the same thing over." He points you to a spot on the barrel but doesn't get up.

locations.[oboz_wronia].visitors.[tomasz.t: Tomasz turns up by the wagons with a blanket over his shoulder and the look of a man who isn't sure he belongs here. "Remember me? The deserter who went the right way. It's worse here than I remembered. But the grub's better than in the forest." He claps you on the shoulder and vanishes among the tents.

locations.[oboz_wronia].visitors.[wedrow.t: Two familiar wanderers sit by the fire with mugs. "People here are killing each other over copper and a rag on a stick," says one. "And this one's seen flying iron." "So what?" "Nothing. Just saying." They nod and finish their drinks.

locations.[obserwatorium].spots.[archiwu.t: The archive is a cellar with shelves of scrolls, tablets and books, every one of them scorched on one side, as if a dragon had been reading them. On one of the maps someone has drawn circles in red ink and written: "Fell here. Fell here. Will fall here." It smells of soot and mouse shit.

locations.[obserwatorium].spots.[kot].sc.t: A big grey tomcat sits on the windowsill and looks at you like an empty bowl. On his collar is a tin tag: "Comet. Do not feed, do not stroke, do not trust."
The cat looks at you like an old crony who owes him a fish. One ear twitches a hair's breadth, which in a cat means emotion beyond all control.
The cat gets up, stretches for show and walks off to the other end of the sill. Meaning: the audience is over.
The cat washes his ear with a paw, with the air of someone who has more important business, and looks out of the window as if you'd never been born.

locations.[obserwatorium].spots.[pomocni.t: A boy in an apron too big for him turns a lantern over in his paws and looks at the sky as if he's counting on his fingers. "You're the one from Głuszec, sir, aren't you? The master says your sort bring bad luck. But the master says that about everything, even the soup. I'll spit over my left shoulder, just in case."
"Ah, you again, sir. The stars won't let me sleep. The master says it's bad luck, but I reckon it's the strong brew."
"I've got my lot: the lantern, the sky and the fear. Any one of them is enough for a whole day."
The lad hugs the lantern to his chest and looks at the sky like a man counting the stars for the hundredth time and still getting a different number.

locations.[obserwatorium].spots.[tablica.t: Scraps of paper hang on the board: "Don't touch the machine", "The cat is not yours", "Whoever nicked my book of reckonings should know I don't count stars, I count grudges." Underneath, someone has smeared a smiling comet in charcoal.

locations.[obserwatorium].spots.[taras]..t: From the terrace you can see all of the Glass Hills: the burnt land, the glittering fields of shards and, far off under the sky, a dark patch where nothing grows. The wind whistles through the bent plates of the telescope.

locations.[obserwatorium].spots.[wartown.t: The sentry leans on the gate and squints toward the burnt land. "I've seen nothing, I've heard nothing. But if I see a red cloak, I'll shut the gate first and maybe think afterwards."
"Oh, it's you again. I don't sleep either. Because if I nod off, I'll wake up in another century, God forbid."
"Nothing happens here, and that's the worst of everything that happens here."
The sentry scratches at his helmet so hard they could hear it in the cellar, and goes back to staring at the burnt land.

locations.[obserwatorium].visitors.[hier.t: Hieronim's lad comes down from the tower, puffing as if he'd been running. "The master asks you to drop by. He says it's time for preparations, and he doesn't like saying things twice." The lad vanishes into the kitchen.

locations.[opuszczony_klasztor].hint.t: a bell tower without a bell, four days from the walls

locations.[opuszczony_klasztor].spots.[k.t: The informer slumps against a pillar, the guard sits down beside him and says nothing. The cloisters are quiet again, only the echo takes a long while to die.
You wake in the monastery garden, under a rose bush, with a bruised neck. Someone has left a jug of water and a heel of bread beside you.
You jump out of a window into the garden, and the shouting follows you down the corridors. The chase isn't eager: they'd rather remember your face than run after your legs.
Someone is lurking in the cloisters, and not just one. An informer in a cloak and two guards with cudgels step out from under the arches as if they'd known about you for a long time.
The crypt is empty. All that's left is a chest-shaped patch in the dust.

Under the altar there's a trapdoor, under the trapdoor stairs, and at the bottom of the stairs a chest marked with the order's sign. The nuns left here what was meant to wait out the war. It sat it out. The war isn't over yet.

locations.[opuszczony_klasztor].spots.[r.t: A long table, benches, a cross on the wall and the smell of old wax. On the table stands a bowl someone washed not long ago, and that someone doesn't want you asking about it.
At night you can hear murmured prayers in the monastery, but they aren't prayers, only wind in the empty case of an organ whose pipes were taken away long ago.
Someone has left fresh bread for you in the refectory, without a word. Under it, a note: "For what you did. Don't ask what." The handwriting is shaky but stubborn.
At dusk the sun comes through the stained glass and pours across the floor like spilled wine. For a moment the monastery looks as if someone still lived in it.

locations.[ostatnia_strazica].hint.t: a tower on the ridge, two days from Starwatch

locations.[ostatnia_strazica].spots.[mar.t: Both lie at the foot of the wall. There's half a sack of hardtack left, so that's something.
You wake under the wall with a lump on your head and a lighter purse. The marauders have moved on.
You get down off the ridge over the scree. Behind you, you can hear they've counted it as a victory and are happy with it.
Below the tower on the ridge sit two men armed with whatever the old garrison left behind. One is gnawing hardtack, the other is whetting a knife on a stone, and neither is doing it for comfort.

locations.[ostatnia_strazica].spots.[str.t: The watchtower stands on the edge of the burnt land, alone, like a finger stuck up out of the ground. The walls are cracked, the gate is shut, but the smoke from the chimney says someone is holed up here all the same. Over the gate hangs a banner with the Empire's arms, slashed across.

locations.[ostatnia_strazica].spots.[szc.t: In the watchtower wall, between two stones, gapes a crack. Someone has stopped it with a rag, the way you'd stop a hole in a barrel. Under the rag are a bottle, a rolled bandage and a little loose coin, most likely put by for a rainy day.
The crack is empty, and the rag lies beside it. There's no telling that anything was ever there.

locations.[ostatnia_strazica].spots.[war.t: A young sentry on the wall gawps into the emptiness, chewing a blade of grass. "I signed up two years back to count enemies. Nobody said they'd be stars. Devil take it."
"Oh, it's you again. Somebody has to keep watch, and I can't sleep anyway."
"I've got my lot: the wall and the crossbow. The rest is none of my business."
The sentry picks between the stones of the wall with the stock of his crossbow and looks like a man counting the hours till his watch ends.

locations.[ostoja_zbojcow].hint.t: smoke over the forest, three days' trail east

locations.[ostoja_zbojcow].spots.[gnat]..t: A skinny figure with a ladle huddles by the cauldron. "Bones, kitchen boy. Was going to be a merchant, but I'd nothing to trade." He nods at the palisade. "Don't go thinking any of this is mine. I only cook here."

"Back, are you? First one ever." Bones stirs the soup. "The chief reads imperial letters, on account of one of the lads knows his letters. They know a thing or two about survivors up north. Not much, but they talk."
"Lately the brigands were saying the Emperor pays for the heads of anyone who's seen wraiths up close. I've seen nothing. I just do the soup." He shrugs.
Bones waves his ladle at you. "Off with you, or my soup'll burn from all your talk."

locations.[ostoja_zbojcow].spots.[obozow.t: The chief topples off his barrel and doesn't get up again. The camp goes quiet. There may be something left in the huts, unless the brigands ate and drank the lot.
You wake under a fence, with no purse and a fresh bruise across your whole face. The chief let you live. Probably wants you to tell folk how you got your arse kicked.
You vault the palisade like your boots are on fire. The chief bellows after you: "I'll get you yet, you little shit!"
Behind a palisade of logs, two huts and one big fire. The chief sits on a barrel like it's a throne, chopping meat with an axe. He stops when he sees you. "Well, well. Supper's walked in on its own."

locations.[ostoja_zbojcow].spots.[spizar.t: The larder is bare. All that's left is mice and the smell of old herring.
A trapdoor under the floor of the hut. Under the trapdoor, a larder full of loot: cups, tongs, a few helmets and a box with a sealed letter. The box stinks, but what's in it doesn't.

locations.[palac].hint.t: a roof you can see from anywhere, but nobody goes in

locations.[palac].spots.[brama_palacu].s.t: The palace gate stands open so wide it has to be a trap. The guards don't look at you, they look through you.

locations.[palac].spots.[komnata_tronowa.t: A racket swells outside the window, the kind the palace hasn't heard in a hundred years. The gate grinds, shouts go up below the wall, and you recognise Tomasz's voice: "Open up! In the name of the people nobody counted!" The sentries throw down their weapons, because nobody feels like dying for a throne that can't defend itself. The Emperor listens with a smile, as if hearing a lullaby.

The Emperor slumps onto the throne, quietly, like a man who finally can. The cat settles on his lap and purrs. "Tea... leave the tea." Those are his last words. On the table beside him a cup goes cold, and nobody will touch it.

The Emperor slumps onto the throne, and the pen slips from his fingers. "You'll pay your debt the way I paid mine. In instalments. Only the instalments get paid by other people." He closes his eyes. "Pity I never finished the ledger."
The Emperor slumps onto the throne and stares at the ceiling. "Twenty years. Nobody asked if I wanted it." The cat stretches on his lap as if to comfort him. "Good night."

The Emperor slumps onto the throne, and the cat jumps off his lap. "You want to kill the one who sent you? Go on. Just don't expect it to get better after. I thought so too." He smiles at you with something like respect. "I'm glad it's you. Don't ask me why."

The blade at your belt starts to hum, softly, as if someone had plucked its strings. The light in the chamber shivers, the cat's shadow on the wall swells and vanishes. The Emperor sighs like someone who has waited years to leave a cold room. Nothing touches him. The thread his sleep hung on simply snaps. The pact ends with a soft crack you hear in your bones.

At night the palace looks like a ship the crew has abandoned. The cook opens the kitchen door without meeting your eyes and points at the stairs. Upstairs the footsteps thud too loud, and every corridor smells of wax, fear and cat. There's no guard outside the throne room. Only a door, open a hand's width, and the flicker of a candle.

The door behind you opens quietly. An old soldier from the Last Watchtower walks in, in a cloak that remembers better days, with a knife that remembers even better ones. He doesn't look at you. He looks at the Emperor, the way you look at an enemy you've waited a lifetime to meet. "For those who weren't counted," he says, flatly, like a man reading out a bill.

The chamber goes quiet. The cat sits on the dead Emperor's lap, washing its paw as if nothing had happened. You did nothing, only watched. From below comes the noise of a city that doesn't know yet but is already afraid. You leave the chamber as you found it: with a lamp, a cat and a finished life.

locations.[palac].spots.[schody_sluzby]..t: By day the servants' stairs are full of maids and lackeys running up and down, and gossip outruns them all. Nobody looks you in the face, because nobody wants to be remembered afterwards. The chamber upstairs is locked tight in daylight. Come back at night.

At night the servants' stairs are the one road where nobody asks questions. A footman with a tray passes you and whispers without moving his lips, "I know who you are. Quiet. The stairs listen." He nods up towards the bend, where the throne room waits, and vanishes.
At dusk the stairs smell of onion and sweat. Someone carries a jug, someone scrubs the floor, someone pretends he saw nothing.

locations.[pole_bitwy].hint.t: crows over the field, half an hour from the camp

locations.[pole_bitwy].spots.[pole].scen.t: On the field where someone beat someone yesterday, nobody wins today. What's left are the holes from the standards, broken spears and trampled grass.

locations.[pole_bitwy].spots.[szabrownic.t: The last looter slumps onto his own sack. From the field nobody protests, only the crows change branches. The sacks jingle with other people's rings, buckles and teeth. Gold ones.
You wake in a ditch, with a sore side and a memory of a knife. Someone left a flask of water beside you. Out of pity, probably.
