You bolt, and behind you comes a whistle and laughter. The looters don't chase. They have sacks.
Three shadows with sacks scurry between the broken wagons. One raises his head and whistles, and the others pull knives. Looters don't like witnesses, but they like easy targets.

locations.[pole_bitwy].spots.[woz_szuler.t: You wake under the wheel of someone else's wagon, with an empty stomach and a sore head. Your purse is lighter by exactly as much as the cardsharp thought fair. The wagon stands where it stood.
The wagon's gone. Two ruts remain and one die that nobody bothered to bend down for. It shows a six on every side.
You flee between the broken wagons. Nobody chases you. Behind you there's only the rattle of dice and laughter: Mszczuj is counting how long it took you.

locations.[pole_bitwy].spots.[wrony].sce.t: A flock of crows has gathered on the only tree, arguing about something fiercely. By day they've got work, so they don't bother you, but they don't leave their post either.
At night the crows are silent, which is worse than the cawing. All you hear is the wind in the broken spears and somebody's cough. A man's, one hopes.
The crows are in no hurry to leave. They watch you with polite curiosity, as if counting how much more of the field you'll leave them.
At dusk the crows burst off the tree like one big cloud and settle back down. The whole ritual repeats three times before they calm down.

locations.[pole_szkla].spots.[patrol].sc.t: The patrol lies scattered over the glass like a handful of beads. The chest of shards stands open, but better still, nobody will be describing your mug in a report now.
You wake under a scree of glass, with no weapon in your hand, but still breathing. The patrol took you for dead, or for not worth the bother.
You leap away over the sheet of glass, which creaks like ice. The sergeant bellows orders, the soldiers slip and slide. You barely get away.
Boots crunch on the glassy ground. Three imperial soldiers in red, a sergeant at the front. They're gathering shards into a chest, and they look at you as if you'd stolen them.

locations.[pole_szkla].spots.[szklane_po.t: Here the ground has set into waves of glass, as if someone had poured out a lake and frozen it mid-ripple. Shards stick out of it like teeth: green, blue, red, each one sharp as a splinter. When you bend down, you see a reflection in them that isn't yours.

locations.[pole_szkla].spots.[zbieracz]..t: A peasant in leather gloves pokes around in the glass with a stick and stuffs something into a sack. "Don't touch it, if you value your life. I've been touching it for thirty years and I'm three fingers short. But trade is trade."
"Oh, it's you again. The glass doesn't sleep, so neither do I. I'm three fingers short, but my eyes are fine."
"The field's big, and nobody here gets in anybody's way. Just don't tread on anything that shines."
The gatherer pokes around in the glass with his stick and doesn't look up. The gloves creak, the glass tinkles, and the conversation is over.

locations.[port_rzeczny].hint.t: the smell of tar and fish beyond the west gate

locations.[port_rzeczny].spots.[kantor_p.t: The informer and the big lad lie on the quay, and the river mutters below as if nothing happened. In the informer's pocket you find a note with your description and a scribble: "come back for round two."
You wake on the riverbank, wet and furious. Someone pulled you out of the water and left you to come round. Even the port has some mercy, it seems.
You leap into the dark and hide among the boats. Behind you a splash, a shout and a colourful curse from someone who tripped over a rope.

The smell of tar hangs over the quay. A lean man in a long coat steps out from behind the barrels, a big lad with a club behind him who looks like he's had enough talking for one day. "The harbour captain would like a word with you," says the lean one. "Right here, no witnesses."

locations.[port_rzeczny].spots.[nabrzeze.t: Barges with timber, salt and cargo that's neither one nor the other tie up at the quay. The dockers curse in three languages and never run short of invention in any of them.
At night the port is full of splashing and whispers. Sometimes it's fish, and sometimes something that would rather not show its face.
The skipper slaps you on the shoulder. "So it's you? The one who runs for the scribe? Good. When people are scared, prices go up, and someone like you always comes in handy."
At dusk the mist rises off the river and hides the hulls halfway up. The lanterns blink in the fog like tired eyes.

locations.[port_rzeczny].spots.[przemytn.t: The crates stand open, and the men who guarded them lie around. It smells of tar and blood.
You wake on the quay with a sore neck. The crates are gone, and so is everyone who could tell you what happened here.
You burst out of the warehouse onto the quay. Shouting and clatter behind you, but nobody follows: the smugglers have cargo to mind.
In the warehouse behind the quay a few men are repacking crates, with the ease of men who've done this before. When you open the door, they all turn their heads at once. One reaches for a club.

locations.[przeprawa_szarej].spots.[most.t: By day the bridge is just a bridge: planks, ropes and tar. Across the river stands the chimney of a burnt cottage, stubbornly, as if waiting for further orders.
At night you can barely see the bridge. Something splashes down below, but you'd rather not check what.
The bridge planks creak underfoot. Someone came this way recently and didn't want to be seen: the mud tracks stop at the railing.
At dusk the water turns leaden, and the wind brings the smell of burning from the far bank. The sentries argue whose turn it is on watch.

locations.[przeprawa_szarej].spots.[stra.t: The guard's hut stands empty; a mug and an unfinished patch have been left on the bench. Nothing much, but a man still looks round in case someone's coming back.

locations.[przystan_jarnowo].spots.[nabr.t: Tar steams on the hulls, and the wind carries the smell of salt and burnt wood. The dockers shout at each other across the width of the jetty as if it were the sea.
At night only the watchman and his cat walk the quay. The water mutters under the jetty as if counting the boats.
On the quay someone breaks off a chat and turns your way. "That the one who runs errands for the captain?" He gets a few nods in answer and not a single smile.
At dusk the lamps on the quay come on one by one, in the order the shifts end. The gulls go back to the masts to sleep in company.

locations.[przystan_jarnowo].spots.[stol.t: Sheets of paper lie held down with stones, each with a tar stain on the edge. The wind peeks under the paper and leaves, disappointed.
Nobody sits at the table at night. The sheets are packed away in a chest, and only the wind pushes a forgotten crumb of charcoal across the top.
Brygida stops drawing and looks at you over her shoulder. "Heard you've been tidying up around here," she says, with neither praise nor sneer in her voice. She goes back to her charcoal.
At dusk the charcoal leaves dark marks on your hands, and the island behind you goes the colour of stone. Someone brings a lamp and sets it on the corner of the table.

locations.[przystan_jarnowo].visitors.[g.t: A lad in a grey jerkin stops you on the quay, out of breath from running. "The hetman is asking after a stranger with no colours who runs errands for the captain. His tent's in the camp, over the hill by the bay. When you've got the time, sir. And you'd better have it."

locations.[rozbita_lodz].hint.t: a rusty shape below the Glass Hills, two days from Starwatch

locations.[rozbita_lodz].spots.[gwidon]..t: A man with a spyglass and a notebook sits on the hull. "Gwidon. I gather light." He raises the spyglass to his eye and lowers it again. "This ship fell here a hundred years ago. Or yesterday. The calendar's in a mess."
"You're back. I've noticed the stars above us don't shine in the same places any more. Someone's moving them." Gwidon counts something on his fingers. "Or we're the ones moving."
"They say wraiths aren't demons. I say wraiths are guards. And a guard always serves someone." Gwidon doesn't look at you. "Ask the Emperor about it, if you ever meet him."
Gwidon raises a finger. "Quiet. I'm counting now. Sorry, that wasn't meant for you."

locations.[rozbita_lodz].spots.[kadlub]..t: The lights go out one by one. In the hull there's only cold left, and a silence so deep you can hear the blood in your veins.
You wake on a dune of glass, with the hull standing on the horizon. Someone has left you water. You won't get to thank them.
You tumble out of the hull's shadow, and behind you flash lights that don't give chase, just remember.
A hull sticks out of a dune of glass, long as a barn, its edge melted like a candle. Little lights flash and small figures flicker all around. They're making sure nobody sees too much.

locations.[rozbita_lodz].spots.[wlaz].sc.t: The chamber is empty. Only dust.

In the hull you find a hatch that opens with a groan, as if it wanted to say something. Behind it is a cold chamber with metal chests. In one lie things someone once thought valuable: an amulet, a buckle, woven links.

locations.[ruiny_fortu].hint.t: a tower above the crossing, the one with no roof

locations.[ruiny_fortu].spots.[baszta_wi.t: The tower looks out over the river, the two camps and the burnt village. From here it all looks almost peaceful, if you don't look too closely.
At night from the tower you see only sparks and darkness. The sentry talks about stars, but that must be a joke: the sky is black as pitch tonight.

From the top of the tower you can see both camps at a glance. The sentry looks into the distance, then at you. "You see everything from up here. Like the fact that nobody's doing a thing around here except you."
At dusk both camps light their fires. From above it looks almost cosy.

locations.[ruiny_fortu].spots.[brama_for.t: The fort's gate is two charred beams and a sentry pretending to guard it. Everyone knows the fort has been gone for ages, but nobody has the nerve to tell it.

locations.[ruiny_fortu].spots.[patrol_ce.t: The last pikeman drops onto the courtyard. They leave behind belts, bolts and a smell of powder mixed with sweat.
You wake in a ditch, sand under your back, sky above your head. The patrol moved on, deciding you were unimportant.
You vault the wall at the last moment. Behind you a shout and a bolt that hits the wall where you stood a moment ago.
In the fort's courtyard you meet an imperial patrol in full kit. Pikemen block your way, a crossbowman aims from the roof. Nobody says "halt", because nobody intends to wait for an answer.

locations.[ruiny_stacji].hint.t: a tower of cold stone, four days from Starwatch

locations.[ruiny_stacji].spots.[archiwum.t: The archive is empty. The shelves stand like the ribs of a dead animal.

Behind iron doors are shelves full of glass tablets. Most of them crumble under your fingers, but a few things have survived: a half-plate on a stand and a handgun in a chest, with a note: "careful, it bites."

locations.[ruiny_stacji].spots.[jaromir].t: In the entrance hall sits a man in a cloak of red broadcloth. "Jaromir. Keeper. I make sure nothing gets out and nothing gets in. Begging your pardon, something just did." He smiles uncertainly.
"You're back. Listen, I've been here twenty years, and only once have I seen a living man from outside." Jaromir touches the wall with his palm. "The walls are warm at night. Nobody knows why."

"At the bottom of it all there's something that works away under the city. They say it's a heart, but a heart doesn't make that much noise. The Emperor owes it a debt, and whoever runs up a debt in a place like that doesn't pay in gold." The keeper blinks nervously.
Jaromir goes back to his book. "I don't understand the question. Good day to you."

locations.[ruiny_stacji].spots.[sala_str.t: The wraith folds up like a badly pitched tent, and the wisp goes out in its shadow. The hall falls silent. There's some relief in it, and a little fear of the next floor.
You wake at the foot of the tower with a copper ring on your chest. You don't remember how you got it, or how you got here.
You run down stairs that won't end. Nothing is chasing you, and yet you feel breath on the back of your neck.
The tower smells of cold and copper. In the hall below stands something that doesn't breathe, and beside it flickers a wisp. You can't tell which of them noticed you first.

locations.[ruiny_straznicy].hint.t: black walls on a hill, a day's walk south

locations.[ruiny_straznicy].spots.[kamie.t: A raven sits among the stones, looking wiser than half the Ford. It looks you in the eye and caws once, dull. Maybe a greeting. Maybe an omen. Best spit over your left shoulder.
The raven again. It caws, and this time it's clearly holding something against you.
The raven turns its tail on you. It has business of its own.

locations.[ruiny_straznicy].spots.[oboz_.t: The fire burns low, the barrel turns out to be empty, and you're the only one still standing. Got to say, the evening didn't start too badly.
You wake in the burdock, two groats short and with a lump the size of half your head. The brigands had mercy, or no time. You'd rather not know.
You jump through a breach in the wall and run till you get a stitch. Behind you someone curses so juicily it's almost a shame not to go back.
Under a crumbling wall there's a fire, three fellows round it and a barrel. One of them spots you first: "Who the fuck's this?"

locations.[ruiny_straznicy].spots.[ruiny.t: A worn little plate stamped with the watchtower's mark sticks out of the rubble. Someone left it here or lost it, and won't be coming back for it.

Deeper in stands a wall with a mark carved into it. You put the amulet to it, and the stone trembles as if waking from sleep. The mark fits line for line, but the door doesn't open. Not yet. The old guard was right.
Black walls jut from the hill like rotten teeth. The gate hangs on one hinge, and through the holes in the roof you can see stars, though it's day. Inside it stinks of old burning and carrion.

locations.[ruiny_straznicy].spots.[warto.t: In the shadow of the fallen gate sits an old man in a rusty helmet, guarding a doorway with no door. "Halt! Password!" When you say you don't know it, he nods approvingly. "Good. Nobody does."
The old man salutes you with a stick. "Czcibor, sentry. Twenty years I've stood here and nobody's come to relieve me. But nobody's got in either, so the watch goes on."
"The brigands come by of an evening for bricks to ring their fire. I give them the password, they give me bread. It's a fair deal." Czcibor winks at you.
The old man eyes you suspiciously. "You again? The password's been changed, only nobody told me what to." He turns to the wall and goes on guarding.

locations.[spalona_osada].hint.t: smoke over the valley, two days north of Głuszec

locations.[spalona_osada].spots.[piwnica.t: The cellar is as empty as an innkeeper's conscience. The wind whistles in the chimney.
A cellar hatch sticks out of the Burnt Ground. Inside are dried herbs, jars and a chest of keepsakes left by the people who lived here. They're no use to them any more, but plenty to you.

locations.[spalona_osada].spots.[wit].sc.t: A peasant in a sooty sheepskin sits on a fallen beam, gnawing a bone. "Chwalisław. I lived here, before they came with swords, and then with torches." He holds out the gnawed bone to you. You politely decline.

"You're back? Good. At least someone's seen what they did to us." Chwalisław looks over the ruins. "They were after the smith. The one who made a pistol out of a wraith's pipe. They found the smith, the pistol and the whole village into the bargain."
"Plenty of folk think the Emperor is evil. The Emperor's a clerk. Evil has a face of black glass, and it doesn't come with a sword." Chwalisław falls silent, as if his own words frightened him.
Chwalisław gives you a pitying look. "I'll say no more. I wouldn't have lived this long if I talked."

locations.[spalona_osada].spots.[zgliszc.t: The last of the looters slumps into the soot. The ruins go quiet.
You come round next to a charred fence. You get back your breath and your shame, but not your purse.
You run down the hillock with curses raining after you.
Charred beams, chimneys sticking up, and men in the remains of uniforms raking through the ashes. Searching, or rather looting. One of them straightens up and reaches for his knife.

locations.[spalona_wies].hint.t: smoke over the valley, a village that isn't there

locations.[spalona_wies].spots.[chata_ko.t: The smith's cottage is now a chimney, an anvil and a heap of slag. The anvil is the only thing in the village nobody stole, because it's too heavy.
At night the anvil gleams in the moonlight. A hammer with a cracked handle lies in the ash.
Someone has managed to light a fire in the ruins of the cottage. Two soldiers from opposing armies stand there, not looking at each other. One passes the other a mug, but neither would admit to it.
At dusk the wind howls in the chimney as if someone were calling from far off.

locations.[spalona_wies].spots.[mul_na_z.t: You wake in the ash, with a lump the size of a cabbage. The cabbage is gone, by the way. The mule stands over you chewing, and the marauders are arguing over a knife by the barn.
A garden bed eaten down to bare earth and some hoofprints are all that's left. Behind the cottage someone has thrown a fishbone, but the mule had nothing to do with that.
You run behind the burnt barn. The marauders don't chase you, because they'd have to leave the mule, and the mule is dinner. When you turn round, Emperor is still eating.

locations.[spalona_wies].spots.[studnia].t: The well stands in the middle of the burnt market square with a bucket on a chain. Around it, circles of dry earth.

locations.[spalona_wies].spots.[zasadzka.t: All that's left of the scouts are maps, notes and a smell of powder that won't air out for a long time.
Darkness, a ringing in your head, charred rafters above you. Someone dragged you out from under the wall and left you in the shade. At least you're alive.
You run across the ruins with a ball whistling over your head. Whatever you did here, the Jarnowians will remember your face.
Behind a ruined wall someone has already laid out a bow and a handgun. Jarnowian scouts jump you before you can say "good day". They know it's their ground, and they play by their own rules.

locations.[stara_kopalnia].hint.t: an iron groan from underground, four days from Głuszec

locations.[stara_kopalnia].spots.[rudy]..t: A bearded man with a lamp sits in the mouth of the tunnel. "Red. Miner. The one that didn't cave in." He chuckles like a pot lid rattling. "Once they dug a metal here that sings. Careful, it brings things back."

"You're back? The metal's taken a liking to you." Red nods. "The Imperials threw us out of here, because their master didn't want folk knowing this metal. He said it was a weapon for the gods. I never met any gods. I met the ones who pass themselves off as gods."
"Don't give it to any old smith." Red narrows one eye. "A bungler will waste it, and you won't find another vein like this one."
Red whistles without a tune. "Off you go. If I've got anything important, I'll remember it."

locations.[stara_kopalnia].spots.[sztoln.t: The water in the tunnel goes still, the little lights go out. Something glints at the bottom that might be a vein of ore, or might be a bone.
You came to at the mine entrance, soaked and out of breath. The waters had drawn back a few paces. You didn't beat them; they got bored.
You climb the ladder with your boots full of sludge, and behind you the water takes the shape of claws.
The tunnel goes down into darkness, with water at the bottom. Water so black that only two little lights are reflected in it. Something in it is breathing.

locations.[stara_kopalnia].spots.[zyla]..t: There's nothing more to chip out of the vein.

Past a caved-in gallery a wall comes into view, with a vein of metal gleaming in it, cold and uneven. The metal doesn't rust, doesn't rot, and is heavier than it looks. You chip off as much as you can carry, and the ring of the chisel drowns out a strange whisper in the rock.

locations.[stare_wodociagi].hint.t: stone arches under the town, three days along the trail

locations.[stare_wodociagi].spots.[kanal.t: The channel runs on into the dark as a long corridor. A narrow shaft of light seeps down from above and picks out a dead rat the size of a cat.
At night the channels are full of footsteps nobody is taking. The echo throws them back as if someone more important than you were walking here.
Someone has chalked something on the wall of the channel that looks like your blade. Underneath it says, "He's not afraid of wraiths." Someone added, "But I am."
At dusk the water under the vault runs louder. The echo carries somebody's whisper, but you can't make out the words.

locations.[stare_wodociagi].spots.[sklad.t: The niche is empty, only the stone still sits loose in the wall.
In a niche behind a loose stone lies a box wrapped in canvas. Someone hid it here in a hurry and never came back. Someone stashed their savings here before the war. The war never found them. You did.

locations.[stare_wodociagi].spots.[szczu.t: The ragamuffins lie among the sacks, and the water quietly washes away the traces.
You wake at the edge of the channel, soaked, with somebody else's jacket over your shoulders. Someone evidently decided you deserved a bit of mercy.
You run over slippery stones, the shouting carrying after you, multiplied by the walls. You come out into the light before they can catch you.
In a wider channel a few ragamuffins are laying out sacks and clubs. They don't look like people who enjoy surprises, let alone guests.

locations.[stary_mlyn].spots.[mlyn].scen.t: The mill wheel stands still, and the water barely stirs beside it. Inside it smells of dust, musty grain and cold stone.
At night the mill is dark and empty, only the boards groan in the wind. The light you saw here is gone.

After dark something inside flares with a pale, cold light. You follow it up the creaking steps, and it backs off a step, like a dog that wants to be chased. In a corner, under the cogwheel, lies a shard of dark glass, pulsing.

locations.[stary_mlyn].spots.[zona].scen.t: The miller's wife peels turnips and talks without looking up. "On Kupała Night Ostap used to drag me down to the mill to float wreaths, and now all he's got in his head is lights in the mill. I say it's his conscience shining. Menfolk would sooner chase ghosts than talk to a woman."
"You again? If you're bored, peel some turnips. The ghosts can wait."
The miller's wife doesn't even look up. "My time runs off like water under the wheel. Come tomorrow, maybe I'll have some news, or maybe just turnips."

locations.[stary_trakt].hint.t: an overgrown road, a day's march south of Głuszec

locations.[stary_trakt].spots.[przydrozn.t: The old road is overgrown with knee-high grass, but the milestones still stand, as if they're still counting steps. On one someone has carved with a knife: "This way they went for the stars." Beside it, with another knife, a correction: "This way they went and never came back." Someone else spat underneath.

locations.[stary_trakt].spots.[rozbity_w.t: The old road runs off both ways, empty enough, but along the edges the grass lies flattened, as if someone dragged something heavy through here. You find nothing more, only the back of your neck itches, as if someone's out looking for you.

In the gully past the bend lies an overturned wagon with a wheel torn off. Around it are boot prints, ruts in the mud and a dried stain you'd do better not to touch. No sign of the goods, but someone has cut a mark into the side with a knife: three strokes across. The mark of people who ran, not people who died.

locations.[stary_trakt].spots.[sakwa_pod.t: Under a collapsed footbridge, on a hook driven into a beam, hangs a leather saddlebag. Someone hid it here before the road grew over and plainly never came back. Inside are bandages, herbs and a handful of groats, all quite dry.
The hook hangs empty, and water drips under the bridge. Someone has already taken the saddlebag. You, as it happens.

locations.[stary_trakt].spots.[wedrowiec.t: A wanderer sits on a milestone chewing hardtack with the face of a condemned man. "I'm going to the Ford. Or from the Ford. In this damned drizzle it's all one: mud everywhere, and they'll fleece you at the toll either way."
"Ah, it's you. My leg's throbbing, so I'm sitting. If I weren't sitting, it'd throb anyway, only on the move."
"I've found what I was after: a seat. If you want to go on, the road's still there. Only the mud changes."
The wanderer crunches his hardtack and pays you no mind.

locations.[stary_trakt].spots.[wilki_tra.t: Both lie in the ruts. The pelts would be worth having, but you can't be bothered to skin them, and winter's a long way off.
You wake in the ruts, covered in slobber, with the skin scraped off your back. The wolves have gone, either because they'd had their fill or because they took pity on you.
You back away slowly, the way they taught you: don't run, don't turn round. The wolves were taught something else, so they run. You get up onto a stump faster than you thought you could.
The Old Road is so overgrown a wagon couldn't squeeze through, but the wolves managed fine. Two of them stand in the ruts and look at you like a dinner that walked up on its own.

locations.[stocznia].spots.[proch_w_szop.t: The shed goes quiet. The powder sacks lie where they were. Just as well nobody fired any closer.
Darkness, somebody's boot, the sharp smell of powder. You wake on the jetty with a sore shoulder, and the watchman's cat sits on your chest, staring at you resentfully.
You burst out of the shed and duck behind the slipway. A shot hits a jetty post and the Shipyard erupts in shouting, but nobody chases you: everyone's got work to do.
Two Jarnowians in grey jerkins are packing sacks in the powder shed. One looks at you too long. "This shed's not for outsiders." The other reaches for a handgun.

locations.[stocznia].spots.[szkielet_lod.t: The frame of a new boat sticks out of the slipway like a whale's ribs. The carpenters knock away with their axes and curse the damp timber.
The Shipyard is quiet at night, only the wind hunting for gaps in the freshly hewn planks.
A carpenter props his axe against the slipway and winks at you without a word. "Heard you fix things," he says, and goes back to work. Around here that counts as respect.
At dusk the carpenters put down their tools and look at the boat frame as if checking it's still standing.

locations.[targ_pod_murem].spots.[plotki.t: A row of stalls runs along the wall, selling goods that belonged to somebody else just last night. The market women squabble over places, and every place has its price.
At night they trade in whispers under the wall. Somebody offers you something you can't see, and you can't help feeling it'd be wiser to buy.

The talk dies down in the market as you come near. Somebody whispers: "That's the one from the board." Somebody else: "From the scribe." They point you out to each other like a two-headed calf at a fair.
At dusk the traders pack up their goods faster than a guard can ask where they got them.

locations.[targ_pod_murem].spots.[przeku.t: The cutthroats lie among the crates. The market woman stares at you in disbelief and, which rarely happens, says nothing.
You wake on the cobbles, horses' hooves right by your head and the smell of rotten apples in your nose. The market woman lays a wet rag on your forehead. "Told you it was no day for shopping."
You dive between the stalls, apples rolling over the cobbles behind you. The cutthroats curse but won't follow into a crowd that might remember them.

It suddenly gets crowded at the market woman's stall: two big lads have blocked the way with crates. One holds a cudgel like a spade handle, the other rolls a gaming die across his fingers. The market woman, who a moment ago was shouting down the whole market, goes quiet.

locations.[trakt_kupiecki].spots.[pielgr.t: The pilgrim sits on a stone by the road and seems to know every saint by name. "Neighbours, son, are the heaviest cross. Mine moves the field boundary a furrow over every year, and come Sunday he's first in church. That's why I walk the world. Out here, at least, there are no boundaries."
"Oh, it's you again. Come with questions about the sky, have you? I don't know what goes on up there. All I know is, when it crackles I pray, and when it doesn't, I pray all the more."
The pilgrim waves you off. "I'm working here: sitting and resting from work. If you want to help, get out of my light."

locations.[trakt_kupiecki].spots.[rozboj.t: Both of them lie in the grass. You leave their clubs where they fell, so nobody thinks it was a good idea.
You wake in a ditch with a lump on your head and the memory of a kick. The robbers have gone on their way, since, as it turned out, there was nothing to take.
You turn back to the road. Behind you somebody bellows that it's not worth it, and it's hard to say whom he means.

A few dozen paces off the road the bushes rustle too loudly. The end of a club pokes out of them, and there's whispering. "That's the one with the purse." "How d'you know?" "He walks like he's got one."

locations.[trakt_kupiecki].spots.[zwiado.t: The scouts are gone, the fire's cold. You know what you needed to know, and the rest is their business.
By the dead campfire you can still see hoofprints and two hollows where men sat not long ago. They'll likely be back after dusk.

locations.[twierdza_graniczna].hint.t: a wall on the horizon, four days from the Ford

locations.[twierdza_graniczna].spots.[br.t: The gate falls silent. The sergeant lies on his own shield, and someone slides off the wall into the grass like a wet rag. You can go in.
You wake outside the wall, where nobody can see you. You don't know who carried you out, but he smells of rotgut and fresh-cut wood.
You scramble down the stones under a hail of arrows. You run till your lungs give out and only slow down in the forest.
A wall higher than the tallest birch and a gate half caved in. Behind it, movement: an imperial patrol with a sergeant at its head and an archer on the wall. Looks like they were waiting.

locations.[twierdza_graniczna].spots.[mi.t: Under the gate sits a customs man, old as the wall, with a seal hung round his neck. "Everyone pays duty, even ghosts. Ghosts don't pay, but I write them down." He enters you in a ledger you don't get to read.

"You came back. Nobody's come back to me in a long while." Mirosz turns a page. "The Emperor shut the border because he dreamed something. What, I don't know, but after what I see over the mountains at night, I pity him."

"Things have come through this gate that no scribe will write down. One of them, with a face like a mirror, bought two apples off me and paid in silver I've never seen." He shows you the coin. It's cold, though it lay in his fist.
Mirosz doesn't look up. "Pay or move on. Ledgers don't write themselves."

locations.[twierdza_graniczna].spots.[zb.t: The armoury smells of rust. There's nothing else here.
Down in the vaults, an armoury: rusty halberds and a few better things that survived under grease. Someone's been here before you, but not everything was worth carrying off.

locations.[ulfgrod].spots.[fontanna].sce.t: The fountain splashes lazily while the traders around it shout at one another. Somebody tries to sell you a sure piece of information for a groat, and an unsure one for half.
At night the fountain murmurs too loudly. Somewhere round the corner somebody laughs, too briefly.

At the fountain somebody strikes up a conversation: "You're the one sorting things out for the scribe?" It gets roomier around you, the way it does around someone nobody wants to touch: not from fear or respect, just in case.
At dusk the square empties in half a breath. The lamplighters light their tallow lamps and curse the price of tallow.

locations.[ulfgrod].spots.[karczma].ambu.t: That's that. Those two won't rob anybody else, at least not here and not today. Somebody in the tavern looked out, saw what was going on and shut the door again.
Someone hits you on the back of the head and the world goes dark. You wake in the gutter, sore all over. A note lies on your chest: "Thanks for your cooperation."
You dive into a side alley. Behind you someone shouts: "And don't come back, or I'll rob you properly!" You snort with laughter in spite of yourself.

At the tavern door you bump into two lads who rub against you far too often for such a wide street. One apologises in a voice that has apologised a hundred times already. The other stops smiling when his hand stops in your pocket.

locations.[ulfgrod].visitors.[smyk_wola].t: Nipper sprouts up next to you as if from underground and tugs your sleeve. "Hey, mister. I hear you've got your paper now. Then come see me before somebody takes an interest in it. The paper is everything, but only till the first check." And he vanishes as if he'd never been there.

Nipper sprouts up next to you as if from underground and tugs your sleeve. "Hey, mister. They talk a lot about you in the square, and that usually means somebody's already asking. If you want to go where you want to go, get yourself a paper and come see me. The paper is everything." And he vanishes as if he'd never been there.

locations.[wilczy_brod].spots.[gospodyni.t: The farmwife throws her hens a handful of grain and curses the neighbour over the fence. "Her over the fence is marrying off her daughter, sir, and she hasn't asked me to the wedding. Just as well, or I'd throw salt on her doorstep. A wedding like that's nothing but debts and a brawl."
"Oh, you're back. If I had anything to tell you, I'd have told you. At least the hens keep up their end of a conversation."
The farmwife waves you off without looking. "Go on, go on. Can't you see a hen's laid an egg? It's a feast day."

locations.[wilczy_brod].spots.[straznik].t: The sentry leans on the palisade, picking his teeth with a splinter. "Frost on the pikes since first light, fuck me. Pay's three months overdue, and the quartermaster says the Emperor's skint too. Me, I believe in rotgut. At least it warms you, and you can buy it."
"You again? My relief's not here yet, so I'll talk to anyone, even you. I'll tell you something: this palisade's only standing because nobody's tried storming it yet."
The sentry doesn't even turn his head. "I don't talk on watch. Unless somebody stands me a rotgut. Then I talk. Not on watch, though."

locations.[wilczy_brod].spots.[woz_ostro.t: A familiar wagon with a cracked wheel stands by the gate, and a plump merchant greets you with a deep bow. "Turns out you're a man of your word. I need someone with iron at his belt as far as Stone Pass. I'll pay, if I don't forget."

Ostromir's wagon stands by the gate again, with a patched shaft and half its cloth. The thugs took what they could carry and left the rest in the ditch along with the wagon. The merchant has somebody else's boots on his feet, and this time he doesn't bow. "Two of them. Two, with pitchforks. And me paying for iron."

Ostromir's wagon stands by the gate again, and the horse looks more worn out than the merchant. "Three days I waited. On the fourth I set off alone, got as far as the first little bridge, took a look at the bushes and turned back."

locations.[wilczy_brod].spots.[zona_bork.t: Borek's wife draws water and even hums to herself. "Lame, but home. Sits by the stove cursing his leg, the sheep, the frost and me. Good that he curses. A quiet Borek, God forbid, that's as good as fished out of the water dead."

Borek's wife draws water and even hums to herself. "Came back in one piece, only hungry as a wolf and sulking at the whole world. Sits by the stove counting his sheep out loud and shovelling down his third bowl of porridge. Believe me, it beats silence."
"You again. Borek snores so hard the well shakes, but God repay you all the same. Just don't tell him I said so."
Borek's wife waves at you over her bucket. "I've got my lot: water, sheep, husband. In that order, if it's gratitude we're talking. Stand aside, or you'll get splashed."
Borek's wife hauls her bucket and pays you no mind. "If you're after soup, come tomorrow. Today I'm cooking for my man and nobody else."

locations.[wilczy_brod].visitors.[zebrak.t: A lame beggar sits down by the gate. "Spare a coin for an old soldier? I left a leg at Bloody Meadow, and the Emperor gave me a medal for it. I drank the medal, never got the leg back." He doesn't wait for an answer and vanishes into a crowd that isn't there.

locations.[wilczy_las].spots.[drwal].sce.t: The woodcutter hacks at a stump till the chips fly. "The imperial chancery sent me a pen-pusher saying I've to pay the imperial treasury for clearing land. For trees that grew all by themselves, damn his hide! Devil take him, inkpot and all."
"You again? Take that sword of yours somewhere else, you'll scare my logs."
The woodcutter raises his axe and brings it down without a word. Chips fly. Talk's over.

locations.[wilczy_las].spots.[legowisko].t: The last boar slumps into the leaves, foam on its snout. It smells of blood and pine needles here, and you smell worse.
You wake in the ferns with your head ringing and a tusk mark on your thigh. Someone dragged you away from the lair before you became dinner. Who? You don't ask.
You run down the slope, branches cracking behind you. The boar doesn't come after you. It couldn't give a shit about you, and that suits you fine.
In the thickets of Marchwood the earth is rooted up, the moss torn off, and the bushes reek of sour musk. A boar. And not alone: behind it something else shuffles and growls.

locations.[wilczy_las].spots.[polana].sc.t: The glade's trampled down to bare earth. The herbs you came for are gone, and the new ones haven't come up yet.
The glade smells of resin and something bitter as wormwood. You crouch in the wet ferns and pick the herb that innkeepers call a cure and barber-surgeons call a weed.

locations.[wilczy_las].spots.[slady].sce.t: Past the glade the ground is churned up by sheep's hooves, and among them run the prints of heavy boots. Further on the prints sink deeper, as if someone was walking loaded down. Or carrying someone. The trail turns towards the old walls on the hill.
The tracks are old and smeared by mud, but they still lead one way: towards the walls on the hill.

locations.[wilczy_las].visitors.[mysliwy.t: A hunter crawls out of the undergrowth with a bow on his back and a dead hare at his belt. "Don't shoot at me, and I won't shoot at you. The wolves are jumpy, the wraiths are hungry and folk are stupid. Best to sit at home, but who can sit still." He vanishes among the trees without a word of farewell.

locations.[wir_lysa_skala].spots.[galeri.t: Both go down on the glass, and for a moment the mirrors show only them: the shape of someone who once served, and nothing more. Then the reflections come back to you.
The blow hits you in the chest and the gallery goes dark. You wake at the entrance, and in the glass you see your own face with nothing in it. The guards are back at their posts.
The gallery is empty. In the mirrors you walk alone, and only now and then one of the reflections stops for longer than you do.
You back down the stairs, and from the mirrors someone behind you shouts in your own voice that all you have to do is turn around. You don't turn around.

Beyond the gate the road climbs into the rock and enters a gallery whose walls are black glass, smooth as water in a well. In every mirror someone walks behind you who looks like you, only more tired. At the end of the gallery stand a Servant of the Whirl with an emitter and, beside him, a Glass Warden with a club. Neither says a word.

locations.[wir_lysa_skala].spots.[hala_c.t: The sentries collapse across the floor in heaps of glass and metal. The coils hum higher for a moment, then sink to a lower note.
The club lands once, and a second blow isn't needed. You wake in the corridor, aching, with the print of glass on your cheek.
The hall is silent. The coils hum a lower note, and in a corner lie remains that someone will sweep up one day.
You back out of the hall, and behind you something rustles like an avalanche of glass. The sentries don't move from their places, because the hall is their boundary.
The hall is round as a well, and under the ceiling hang coils of copper and glass, humming a single note. Beneath them stand two glass sentries, still as statues until you take a step.

locations.[wir_lysa_skala].spots.[komnat.t: You return to the hall where you've already stood once. The Being hasn't moved. "Again," she says, without a trace of impatience, as if counting how many times this will happen.

The Being kneels on the glass, and the stars in her face go out one by one, like lamps in an emptying house. "So... this too is a way to get home," she says, and doesn't finish. All that's left of her is a cloak of something that isn't cloth. The frame of the gate stands dark. The rest of her retinue, with no escape and no orders, lays down its arms on the glass or slumps beside its mistress. There's nobody left who would remember that gate.

The Being sinks to one knee, and the light around her flickers as though it couldn't decide which side to leave her on. "Enough," she says. She raises a hand, and the frame of the gate answers with a bright crack. From deep in the rock the rest of her retinue pours out in a panic and throws itself at the Whirl like water down a drain. The Being enters the light last, without looking back. The Whirl closes behind her with a quiet sigh. You're left alone in a hall that suddenly has too much room in it.

The black glass door slides open without a sound. Beyond it is a round hall, and in the middle a frame with no light in it: a gate that you know will never work again. Under it waits the Being without her mask, looking at the severed couplings with the attention of someone counting losses. "You did it," she says, without turning her head.

The black glass door slides open without a sound. In the round hall the light swirls, and under its ring stands the Being without her mask, her back to you. Behind her, at the far end, the frame of the gate runs evenly, ready. "You left it," she says. "Thank you. I won't pretend that means nothing."

Glass hands close over you like a lid. You wake in the corridor outside the chamber door, with the Blade in your hand and silence in your ears. The Being doesn't pursue. She waits where she was, because she knows you'll be back.

locations.[wir_lysa_skala].spots.[pomost.t: The Warden slides into the crack, and the light swallows him without a sound. The Servant falls on the planks of the walkway. The Whirl beneath you slows for a moment, as if it had swallowed.
The blow takes your breath, then your sight. You wake at the start of the walkway, smelling scorched cloth. The walkway holds up better than you thought.
The walkway trembles only under your steps. Below, the Whirl keeps turning, uninterested.
You back away along the walkway, and the beam warms your back before you've cleared the line of fire. Nobody chases you.

The corridor ends in a narrow walkway over a crack where light turns. There's nothing under your feet and nothing overhead, and in the middle stands a Glass Warden, with a Servant of the Whirl and his emitter behind him. The walkway trembles as if waiting for a weight.

locations.[wir_lysa_skala].spots.[wejsci.t: Inside, the rock is as quiet as a freshly dug well. Black glass walls run upward, and the light reflected in them is colder than the light you saw outside. Somewhere above, something walks, one step every quarter of an hour.
The glass remembers your steps. Ahead lie the gallery, the hall and the walkway.
Three thresholds behind you. Ahead only the black glass door, with light seeping through it as if from under an eyelid. The Blade at your belt hums a single steady note.
The path leads to the chamber where you've already stood once. The black glass door is ajar, and inside waits someone who has had time to prepare.

locations.[wrak_maszyny].spots.[wrak].sc.t: The machine's tin ribs jut out above you like the bones of a beast nobody has ever seen. You know this chill already. It was there that night on the road.
Inside, the machine is cold as a well, but it smells of something familiar: wet earth and iron. The plates on the walls glow faintly as you come closer and go dark as you back away.

locations.[wrak_maszyny].spots.[zlomiarz.t: The scrap man is beating out a piece of tin with a hammer that's probably younger than the tin. "The machine? I know, I know. Don't touch, don't sell, don't ask. I stick to the third one, because the first two don't pay."
"Oh, it's you again. The tin talks to me at night. Thin little voice, but it talks sense."
"The wreck won't strip itself. Get out of my light."
The scrap man taps his tin with the hammer and looks pleased with his work. You won't get any more talk out of him.

locations.[wraki_floty].hint.t: masts sticking out of a reef north of the island, two days by boat

locations.[wraki_floty].spots.[poklad_wr.t: A warship lies heeled over on the reef, its broken mast poking at the sky. Gulls sit in the ribs of the hull and couldn't care less.
At night the wrecks blink with the green glow of rotting wood. The quiet is so thick your own footsteps sound like somebody else's.
An old fisherman sits on the deck with a rod, smiling as if he knew who you were. "Off to the Whirl? Don't mind me, I'm only fishing," he says, and goes back to it.
At dusk the water between the wrecks turns leaden, and the decks creak as if somebody were walking on them.

locations.[wraki_floty].spots.[rabusie_w.t: The looters lie among the splintered planks. The ship groans and shifts a hair on the reef, as if allowing itself a sigh.
You wake in a cabin, against the wall, with a bandage on your head that you didn't put there. There's a flask on the table. Nobody left a note.
You jump to the next wreck over a rotten beam, and the looters stay on the far side of the water. The wind carries their curses until nobody can tell whose they are.
Three men with tar on their faces come out of the wreck. One swings an axe, another points a finger at you. "The wreck's ours. So are the chests. And you're surplus to requirements."

locations.[wraki_floty].spots.[skrzynia_.t: The chest stands open and empty, and the rotten pallet still remembers the shape of somebody else's head.

In a cabin of the wreck, under a rotten pallet, sits a brass-bound chest. The lock has rusted solid, but the plank beneath it split under your knee. Inside lies whatever the captain preferred to take with him rather than leave to the fleet.

locations.[wzgorze_wartownicze].spots.[p.t: The old shepherd lies in the grass counting sheep that probably aren't there. "A hundred and twenty. Or a hundred and nineteen. A wolf took one, but hush, speak of the wolf and he'll come for the rest. Never liked that one anyway."
"Ah, it's you. The sheep snore, so I can't sleep either. A hundred and twenty, I say. Or a hundred and nineteen."
"I've got my job: I lie here. Hard graft, that."
The shepherd rolls over in the grass and grins at the clouds. "I'm counting. Come back in an hour and I'll tell you what I got."

locations.[wzgorze_wartownicze].spots.[s.t: From the top you can see Głuszec laid out like the palm of your hand: smoke from the chimneys, the graveyard, and a red smudge on the road that might be a cloak, or might just be the sunset. Someone has worn a path up here, but the devil knows who or why.

Through a clump of junipers you see a low camp: two horses, three red cloaks and a fire someone is trying to hide under a sheet of canvas. One of them is watching Głuszec through a spyglass. You lie in the wet grass till your elbows go numb, and count: three. A fourth is probably snoring in the tent.

locations.[wzgorze_wisielcow].hint.t: old gallows on the horizon, three days from camp

locations.[wzgorze_wisielcow].spots.[kam.t: The stone circles are older than the gallows, the war and the caretaker. They stand in a ring, and the air between them is thicker, like before a storm.

locations.[wzgorze_wisielcow].spots.[pad.t: Under the gallows there is nobody again but you and those who hang there. The usual old silence settles.
You wake under the gallows with tooth marks on you and cold in your bones. The caretaker hands you water without a word.
You run down the slope, wolves at your back. In the end they give up. Wolves have a rule: you don't chase what's about to carry itself off.
Wolves and one figure with a sack are busy under the gallows. The looter digs in the ground while the wolves look at you with a question in their eyes. Who's feasting today?

locations.[wzgorze_wisielcow].spots.[sta.t: The caretaker sits on a stool, picking his teeth. "All sorts hung here. The worst ones had the best names."

There are more on the gallows now. The caretaker counts on his fingers, loses track and starts over. "Thirty-two. Haven't had so many at once since the old king. We ran out of rope, the cord went for buckets." He looks at you without anger. "Somebody had to show them the way. Uphill, there's always somebody who shows the way."
At night the caretaker doesn't sleep. He sits and listens to the wind playing on the ropes. "They tell all sorts of things. I don't listen. I just watch."
The caretaker looks up as you approach. "I've heard of you. Three cases on the front, and nobody hanged. Rare thing." He says it with honest surprise, as if it were the best news in ten years.
At dusk the caretaker lights a lamp by the gallows. No telling what for: nobody comes here after dark. "For order's sake," he says.

locations.[wzgorze_wisielcow].spots.[szu.t: The gallows stand in a row like beanpoles in a garden. Nobody cuts them down, because nobody wants to admit they were ever useful.

The earth under the oldest gallows has been freshly turned. Somebody buried something here in a hurry and never found the time to come back. Under a thin layer of sand lie a pouch, a grey bundle and a few small things that nobody will be needing any more.

locations.[zapadlisko_ciszy].hint.t: a fog where the birds fall silent

locations.[zapadlisko_ciszy].spots.[gnia.t: The last light goes out, and the hob drops into a crack. The fog thins, and sound comes back into your ears with a painful crackle.
You come round in the fog with no sense of time. You pat down your pockets: everything's there, only there seems to be less of you. Someone carried you out of here, but doesn't want to be known.
You flee, groping your way. The fog lets you go just when you think you'll never get out. Behind you, a giggle you can't hear.
In the Hollow the fog eats up every sound, and something flickers in it: two wisps and a small figure in a cap, giggling without a sound. The fog has a nest, and you're standing in it.

locations.[zapadlisko_ciszy].spots.[niem.t: A man sits on a stone with a finger to his lips and nods to you. He points to his ear, then to the fog, then spreads his hands. Clear as day: here you keep your mouth shut.
The mute knows you and pulls a face without ceremony. He points to his ear, then his mouth, then himself, and turns his back. Meaning: I've nothing to talk about, and you wouldn't hear it anyway.
The mute waves his arms, and from the waving you make out: go your own way. He points at your legs as he does it, as if they were to blame.
The mute puts a finger to his lips and looks at the fog. Meaning: not today.

locations.[zapadlisko_ciszy].spots.[zapa.t: The Hollow is as deep as a giant's well. Fog fills it to the brim and spills over slowly, as if something were breathing. The silence here eats sound the way a bog eats boots.
The air thickens, and the sounds die one after another: first the birds, then the wind, last of all your own footsteps. The fog and the ground run together into one sea of milk.

locations.[zaulek_szklarzy].spots.[kiesz.t: Both lie on the cobbles. The boot is still broken, but nobody minds any more.
You wake on the cobbles, your purse lighter. The thieves are gone, and the glassmaker shuts his shutters so as not to see anything.
You turn back and leave the alley the way you came in. Behind you comes laughter and something that sounds like a lost bet.
The alley is narrow, and two men stand exactly where it narrows. One pretends to mend a boot, the other to be learning how. The purse at your belt suddenly feels heavy.

locations.[zaulek_szklarzy].spots.[praco.t: The alley smells of sulphur, glass and something sweet that turns bitter at the end. The glassmakers size you up like a customer who can be fleeced.
At night only one window is lit in the alley, and a man stands in it staring at a test tube as if it were about to confess something.

The alchemist lifts his head from the retort. "I hear you've been sorting out all sorts of business lately. Maybe you could find time for mine too?" He goes back to stirring as if he hadn't asked at all.
At dusk blue flames flash in the workshop windows, and somewhere deep inside someone coughs long and loud.
